If you are buying a compliant asset with a long term at a pric

t: Can foreigners own property in Japan?
s: Japan lets any foreigner own land outright with no restriction. Bali lets you own none of it. The money still goes to Bali, and the reason is instructive.
b:
Japan is the cleanest counter example to everything people assume about Asian property.

   Japan has no nationality restriction

A foreigner can buy land and buildings in Japan outright, freehold, registered in their own name, with no residency requirement, no quota and no minimum value. You do not even need a visa to buy.

That is a stronger position than Thailand, the Philippines, Vietnam, Malaysia or Indonesia offer.

   So why is the money not all going there?

  Buildings depreciate to almost nothing.   Japanese houses are widely treated as wasting assets with a functional life measured in decades. Value sits in the land, and outside the major cities land has been flat or falling for a generation.

  Demographics.   A shrinking, ageing population means fewer households, and a well documented stock of abandoned homes.

  Rental yields outside the big cities are thin  , and tourism driven short term letting faces its own licensing regime.

  Operating a property remotely is hard   without language and local management.

So you get perfect title on an asset that may not appreciate and may not pay much.

   What Bali offers instead

No ownership, a 30 year term, and a verification burden that falls entirely on you. Against that: tourism demand that recovered past pre pandemic levels, build costs of USD 600 to 1,500 per square metre, low operating costs, and genuinely scarce well zoned coastal land.

The trade is legal certainty for cash flow.

   The lesson

Ownership rights are one variable and people treat them as the only one. Japan proves that perfect title on a depreciating asset in a shrinking market is not automatically better than a limited right on a scarce one with real demand.

That does not make Bali safe. It means the question is not "can I own it" but "what will this be worth, and who can buy it from me, in year twenty five."

   Common questions

    Can foreigners buy property in Japan?
Yes, freehold land and buildings, with no nationality restrict

t: What accounting does a PT PMA need?
s: Monthly filings, quarterly reports and annual statements, owed whether or not the company earned anything.
b:
The formation cost of a PT PMA is quoted constantly. The running cost is quoted rarely, and it is the number that actually matters, because it recurs every year for as long as the company exists.

   The monthly obligations

  Employee withholding tax (PPh 21)  , if the company has staff. Calculated, withheld, paid and reported monthly.

  Withholding on payments to third parties (PPh 23, PPh 4(2))   — services, rent, certain contractor payments. Withheld at source and reported monthly.

  VAT (PPN)  , if the company is registered as a taxable enterprise. Monthly returns, and e faktur invoicing through the system.

  Corporate income tax instalments (PPh 25)  , paid monthly against the eventual annual liability.

Every one of these has a deadline and every missed deadline generates a penalty. They accrue quietly.

   The quarterly obligation

  LKPM   — the investment activity report — is filed quarterly by PMA companies. It reports realised investment and employment.

It is easy to overlook because it is not a tax filing and it comes from a different authority. It is also genuinely enforced, and a company with a history of missed LKPM filings has a standing problem that surfaces at licence renewal.

   The annual obligations

  Corporate income tax return (SPT Tahunan Badan)  , with financial statements attached.

  Financial statements   prepared to Indonesian standards.

  An audit  , where the company exceeds the thresholds requiring one. Below them, unaudited statements are acceptable.

  Annual shareholder meeting (RUPS)   and the minutes, which are a company law requirement rather than a tax one and are frequently forgotten by single shareholder companies.

  Personal returns   for directors and commissioners who are Indonesian tax residents.

   What it costs

A small, low activity PT PMA with a handful of transactions and no staff typically runs   USD 2,000 to USD 5,000 a year   for bookkeeping, monthly filings, LKPM and the annual return.

t: What is healthcare in Bali actually like?
s: Routine care is fine and affordable. Serious care is where people get financially destroyed, and the number is bigger than you think.
b:
Routine healthcare in Bali is better than most people expect and cheap by Western standards. Serious healthcare is where the real financial exposure sits, and it is the thing almost nobody plans for properly.

   The hospitals foreigners use

  BIMC  , in Nusa Dua and Kuta. International standard, priced accordingly. BIMC Nusa Dua was named Medical Tourism Hospital of the Year for Indonesia at the Healthcare Asia Awards 2025.

  Siloam  , several locations. The common choice for expat families who want good care without BIMC pricing.

  Bali International Hospital  , opened in 2024 inside the Sanur special economic zone. This is the most significant change to healthcare here in years. It was built specifically so that complex cases would not all have to fly to Singapore or Australia.

English is spoken at all three.

   What things cost

    Typical cost  
             
  Consultation   USD 40 to 100  
  Emergency room visit   USD 150 to 300  
  Standard room, per night   USD 300 to 500  
  ICU, per night   USD 1,500 to 2,500  
  Minor surgery   USD 500 to 2,000  

Without insurance, a standard emergency case runs   USD 5,000 to 25,000  .

   The number that actually matters

  Medical evacuation to Singapore costs USD 55,000 to 100,000.  

That is the figure that determines whether an accident is a bad week or a life altering financial event. If local care cannot handle your case, that flight is the difference, and nobody has that sitting in a current account.

   What your insurance actually needs

  At least USD 100,000 to 250,000 of medical evacuation cover.   Not general medical cover. Evacuation specifically, named in the policy.

  Direct billing agreements with Bali hospitals.   Without this you pay up front and claim it back later, and private hospitals here will ask for payment or a deposit before treating a serious case. Being right about your entitlement does not help you at 2am.

  Scooter cover, with the licence condition checked.   Many policies exclu

t: What do villa staff cost in Bali?
s: Base salaries are low. The employer obligations on top of them, BPJS and the mandatory annual bonus, are what owners forget to budget.
b:
Staff are usually the single largest fixed cost of running a villa here, and they are owed whether or not a guest ever arrives.

   Monthly base salaries

  Role   Monthly, USD  
             
  Housekeeper   120 to 300  
  Gardener   50 to 120  
  Pool service   30 to 70  
  Security   120 to 200  
  Villa manager   300 to 600  
  Cook   150 to 350  

A typical three bedroom villa runs two to three staff, roughly IDR 7M to 12M a month in base salaries combined.

   The costs on top of base salary

This is where owners get caught out, because these are legal obligations rather than optional extras.

  BPJS contributions.   Employer contributions to the national health and employment social security schemes add roughly 14 percent on top of salary. This is not discretionary for properly employed staff.

  THR.   Tunjangan Hari Raya is the mandatory religious holiday allowance: one full month of salary, paid annually before the holiday. Every employee with twelve months of service is entitled to it, and pro rata below that.

So a team costing IDR 7M a month in base salary is not costing IDR 84M a year. Add BPJS and THR and the real annual figure for a two person team lands closer to   IDR 84M to 100M  .

   Regional minimum wage

Bali sets a provincial minimum wage annually, and regencies set their own within it. Badung, which covers Canggu, Seminyak and the airport side, runs the highest in the province. Paying below the applicable minimum is a labour law problem, not a negotiation.

   Employed or contracted?

Owners sometimes prefer to treat staff as contractors to avoid BPJS and THR. Whether that holds depends on the substance of the relationship, not the label on the paperwork: fixed hours, a single employer, direction and control all point to employment.

Getting this wrong is a labour dispute, and Indonesian labour law is protective of workers. Take local advice rather than assuming the arrangement you prefer is the one that applies.

   Termination is expensive

t: What does it cost to furnish a villa in Bali?
s: Furniture is cheap and good here. What owners get wrong is how fast it wears out and how rarely it is included in a build quote.
b:
Fit out is almost never inside the per square metre construction rate, and it is a substantial line on its own.

   Why buying locally is the right call

Bali has a genuine furniture industry. Teak, suar wood, rattan, terrazzo, upholstery and custom joinery are made here at prices well below Europe, Australia or North America, and the styles suit the climate and the guest expectation.

The workshops around Gianyar and along the Denpasar corridor will build to drawing. Custom is normal rather than a luxury, and the lead times are weeks rather than months.

   Rough budgets

For a three bedroom villa, furnishing to a standard that competes in the nightly rental market:

  Level   Total, USD  
             
  Basic, functional   15,000 to 25,000  
  Good rental standard   25,000 to 45,000  
  High specification   50,000 and up  

That covers furniture, soft goods, kitchen equipment, outdoor furniture, lighting, art and the hundred small things that make a villa photograph well.

Guests judge on photographs. Under furnishing to save USD 10,000 on a property costing hundreds of thousands is a false economy that shows up directly in the nightly rate.

   What wears out, and how fast

This is the part owners underestimate. In this climate:

    Soft goods   (cushions, upholstery, linen, towels) degrade within one to three years
    Outdoor furniture   takes intense UV and rain; two to four years for most
    Mattresses   in high turnover villas need replacing sooner than at home
    Timber   moves with humidity; solid wood survives, veneered board does not
    Air conditioning units   have a shortened life in salt air

Assume a meaningful refresh every two to three years on soft goods, and a full refurbishment cycle around every five.

Solid timber over veneer and MDF, which delaminates. Synthetic outdoor fabrics rated for UV. Stainless or powder coated fittings rather than untreated metal, especially near the coast. Removable, washable covers o

t: Can a foreigner be a director of an Indonesian company?
s: Holding shares is not the same as being allowed to work. Directors without the right authorisation are exposed, and enforcement has tightened.
b:
You can own an Indonesian company as a foreigner. Working in it is a separate question with a separate process, and conflating the two is one of the more common and more serious mistakes foreign owners make.

   Shareholder, director, employee

  A shareholder   owns shares. There is no work authorisation implied and none required, because holding shares is not working.

  A director   —  direksi  — is an officer of the company with legal authority to bind it. A foreign director who is   actively performing the role in Indonesia   requires work authorisation and an appropriate stay permit.

  A commissioner   —  komisaris  — supervises rather than manages. The position is less operational and the requirements differ, which is why some structures place the foreign party here instead.

The distinction that matters is not the title. It is whether you are   performing work in Indonesia  . Signing documents from abroad as a non resident director is a different position from running the business from a desk in Canggu.

   What authorisation requires

  RPTKA   —  Rencana Penggunaan Tenaga Kerja Asing , the foreign worker utilisation plan. The company applies, justifying why the position requires a foreign national, and the plan is approved for defined positions and durations.

  DKP TKA   — the compensation levy payable for employing a foreign worker, charged per position per month.

  The immigration permit   — a work KITAS tied to that position and that sponsoring company. It is not transferable. If you leave the company or the position changes, the permit needs to change with it.

There are also positions closed to foreign nationals entirely, and requirements around Indonesian counterpart staffing depending on the sector.

   What happens without it

This is not a technicality that gets overlooked.

A foreigner working in Indonesia without the correct permit faces immigration consequences ranging from fines to deportation and re entry bans, and the sponsoring company f

t: Can you retire in Bali, and what does it take?
s: There is a route built for it. The requirements are financial rather than age-based, and property gives you nothing.
b:
Yes, and the route is more straightforward than most people expect. It is also not the one most people are told about.

   The route

The   Second Home   family covers financially independent residence with no employer, no business and no family sponsor. The standard tier is commonly cited at either a deposit of around   USD 130,000   in an Indonesian state bank, or qualifying property of around   USD 1,000,000  .

Verify both at the point of filing. These thresholds get revised.

What you get is   five or ten years  , which is what makes it attractive against a permit you renew annually.

   The senior tiers people miss

Within that same family there are dedicated senior or elderly tiers, commonly cited at a minimum age of 55 or 60 depending on the sub index, with income, pension or deposit conditions instead of the full standard threshold.

If you are over 55, ask about these specifically before defaulting to the standard tier. Agents frequently do not mention them.

   The thing that catches people

  Buying a villa does not let you stay.   Property and immigration are unrelated systems in Indonesia. You can own a house here and have no right to be in it beyond a tourist stay.

That surprises people constantly, and it is the most expensive misunderstanding in this market.

   What to think about beyond the visa

  Healthcare.   Routine care locally is fine. Serious care usually means Singapore. Comprehensive international insurance, and check the age limits on the policy before you commit to the move.

  Tax.   Presence, not passport. Beyond 183 days you are an Indonesian tax resident. That has consequences for pension income depending on your home country's treaty position, and it is a conversation to have before you arrive.

  The deposit is not a fee.   Confirm whether it must be maintained continuously, and in what account type, before you move the money.

   If the plan involves buying

Do the visa first. It costs less to discover a problem before you have c

t: Can foreigners buy property in Vietnam?
s: Vietnam grants foreigners 50 years on an apartment. Indonesia grants 30 on a lease. Only one of them has a defined renewal path.
b:
Vietnam is frequently pitched as the next big Southeast Asian market. The ownership rules are the part that gets glossed over.

   What a foreigner can hold

Apartments in approved developments, subject to a quota on foreign ownership within each building and within a given area. Land itself remains under state ownership, with use rights allocated.

The headline figure is   50 years  , renewable in principle. That renewal is the weak point: it is less clearly defined than Indonesia's statutory extension paths for HGB and Hak Pakai, and considerably less certain than a Thai condominium freehold.

   Vietnam against Indonesia

    Vietnam   Indonesia  
                   
  Land   State owned, use rights allocated   Reserved for citizens  
  Foreign holding   Apartments, quota limited   Hak Pakai, lease, HGB via company  
  Term   50 years   30 years, extendable  
  Renewal   Permitted, less defined   Statutory extension paths exist  
  Tourism demand   Growing, domestic heavy   Mature, international  
  Build cost   Low   Low  

Fifty years sounds better than thirty until you ask what happens at the end, and in Vietnam that answer is thinner.

   The practical differences

Vietnam's market is less oriented to foreign short term rental operators. Enforcement of short term letting in apartment buildings has been restrictive in the major cities.

Indonesia's tourism economy is deeper, more international, and better set up for the villa rental model, which is what most foreign buyers here are actually buying.

Vietnam is a growth story. Bali is an income story.

   What to check if you go there anyway

The building's remaining foreign quota, whether the developer has the right approvals, the exact expiry and what the renewal procedure is on paper, and whether short term letting is permitted in that building at all.

   Common questions

    Can foreigners own land in Vietnam?
No. Land is state owned with use rights allocated. Foreigners can hold apartments within quota l

t: What do international schools in Bali cost?
s: From around USD 3,000 to over USD 30,000 a year. And the headline tuition is not the number you actually pay.
b:
For most families, school fees are the single largest line in a Bali budget. Larger than rent, frequently by a wide margin.

   The range

Annual tuition runs from around   USD 3,000   at early years bilingual centres to   over USD 30,000   at premium campuses.

The established international schools sit at roughly   USD 15,000 to 28,000 per student per year  , depending on grade level.

  Green School Bali  , in Ubud, runs approximately   USD 18,000 to 27,000+   a year depending on grade.

  Canggu Community School   runs from roughly   IDR 110 million   for Early Years to   IDR 257 million   for the IB Diploma years.

   The number nobody quotes you

Headline tuition is not what you pay. Once everything is added:

    Annual  
             
  Registration   USD 500 to 2,500  
  Uniforms   USD 150 to 400  
  Transport   USD 1,200 to 3,600  
  Lunch   USD 600 to 1,200  

  All in, budget USD 8,000 to 28,000 per child per year  , depending on school and grade.

For two children at an established school, that is a serious annual commitment before you have paid rent, and it is why family budgets here land in a completely different bracket to single or couple budgets.

   Where the schools are

  The Canggu and Pererenan corridor   serves the entrepreneurial and remote working community. Practical, international, geared to families who arrived recently.

  Ubud   is home to the schools known internationally for creativity and sustainability, Green School most famously.

That geography matters more than people realise.   Pick the school first, then find housing near it.   Bali traffic turns a 12km school run into an hour each way, twice a day, and that decision shapes your entire life here far more than which beach you liked on holiday.

   What to check beyond the fee

    Curriculum and where it leads.   IB, Cambridge and Australian systems are all present, and transferring between them mid stream is disruptive.
    Waiting lists.   Popular year groups fill. Places are

t: How do you get an NPWP in Indonesia?
s: The taxpayer number that most property transactions, company obligations and filings run through. Straightforward to obtain and awkward to be without.
b:
The NPWP —  Nomor Pokok Wajib Pajak  — is Indonesia's taxpayer identification number. Most things that involve the tax office require one, and getting it early is considerably easier than getting it under deadline pressure.

   When you need one

  A titled property transfer.   BPHTB and the seller's disposal tax run through the tax system, and the transaction stalls without a valid registration.

  Declaring rental income   in Indonesia.

  Running a PT PMA.   The company has its own NPWP, and directors and commissioners generally need personal registration.

  Employment   in Indonesia.

  Opening some bank accounts  , depending on the bank and the product.

A straightforward leasehold purchase where you declare no Indonesian income has fewer touchpoints, but if you intend to rent the property out you will need one.

   What you need to apply

  A passport  , valid, with your name exactly as it appears on every other document you will use.

  A stay permit   — KITAS or KITAP — for an individual registration as a resident taxpayer. Registration routes exist for non residents with Indonesian source income, and they work differently.

  Proof of address in Indonesia  , commonly a domicile letter or the SKTT that accompanies a stay permit, or a tenancy agreement.

  For a company  : the deed of establishment, the ministerial approval, the NIB, and identity documents for the directors.

   The process

Registration is handled through the tax office covering your domicile, or online through the Coretax portal. In practice most foreigners use a tax consultant, and it is money well spent — not because the form is difficult, but because a rejected application over a data mismatch costs weeks.

Allow two to four weeks from a complete application. Longer if any document has to be corrected.

   The part that goes wrong

Since the NPWP–NIK integration and the Coretax rollout, the system   matches data strictly and rejects rather than queries  .

t: Can a PT PMA use a virtual office?
s: Cheap and widely used for company formation, and the point where banks and licensing sometimes say no.
b:
A virtual office gives your company a registered address and mail handling without renting premises. It is a legitimate and common choice, with specific limits.

   Why people use them

Company formation requires an address. Renting real premises before the business exists is expensive and often unnecessary, particularly for a holding company or a business whose operations are elsewhere.

A virtual office solves that at a fraction of the cost.

   Where it stops working

  Banking.   Some banks accept a virtual address and some refuse. This is the most common failure point, and it stalls the formation at exactly the step that already causes delays.

  Licensing.   Certain classifications require premises appropriate to the activity. A business that must physically operate somewhere cannot be licensed at a mailbox.

  Domicile letter.   The provider must be able to supply a valid domicile letter for your intended activity and in the right regency. Not all can.

  Project location.   Licensing follows the   project location  , not company domicile. A villa in Pererenan operated by a company registered at a Denpasar virtual office is still a Bali project needing Bali compliant zoning and permits for that parcel.

That last point catches property related companies constantly. The virtual office does not move where your business actually happens.

   What to ask before committing

  Can you provide a domicile letter for my specific KBLI classification?
  Which banks have opened accounts at this address recently?
  Is the address in the regency my project actually sits in?
  What happens at renewal, and what does it cost?
  Do you handle official correspondence, and how quickly do I get it?

Get the banking answer with specifics. "Yes, banks accept us" is not the same as naming banks that opened accounts this year.

   When to take real premises

If the business physically operates somewhere, if the classification requires suitable premises, or if you have already been re

t: Can you legally work remotely from Bali?
s: Yes, and there is a specific permit for it. Most people arrive on the wrong one.
b:
Yes, legally, on a defined route. The problem is that most people work here on a tourist status, which is not a grey area.

   The right permit

  E33G   covers a foreign national who stays employed by, or contracted to, a company established outside Indonesia, and wants residence here without becoming locally employed.

The published criteria are specific:

  A genuine employment or consulting agreement with a   foreign   company
  Minimum annual income commonly cited at   USD 60,000  
  General living funds, commonly cited around USD 2,000
    No income from Indonesian entities at all  

It runs one year and renews while the arrangement and the income continue.

   What it does not cover

It is not a general freelancer permit. If you cannot document both the foreign employment relationship and the income level, you likely do not qualify, whatever an agent tells you.

It also does not permit any Indonesian sourced income. Take on a local client and you are outside the terms.

   The mistake almost everyone makes

Working on a visitor status. A visa on arrival gives 30 days plus one extension. It permits tourism and meetings. It does not permit work, and the fact that your employer is abroad does not change that.

This is enforced. It is not a technicality.

   The part nobody plans for

  Tax residence follows presence, not your visa.   Past 183 days in a year you are an Indonesian tax resident, even though every dollar you earn is foreign.

This is the single most misunderstood point among remote workers here, and it is worth a conversation with a tax adviser before you cross that line rather than after.

   If you are considering property

Buying does not give you the right to stay, and the E33G is not framed as a route to permanent residence. If long term security is the goal, [look at the routes that do lead there](/visas/kitap itap indonesia/) before you commit capital.

   The permit that made it lawful

Before the E33G existed, effectively everyone working r

t: Do Australians pay tax twice on Bali property?
s: Indonesia taxes the property income first. Australia assesses your worldwide income and gives credit. Relief is not automatic.
b:
Australians are the largest foreign buyer group in Bali, and this is the question most of them get wrong in the same direction.

   How the treaty allocates

Income from   immovable property   is generally taxable in the country where the property is. That gives   Indonesia primary taxing rights   over rental income from a Bali villa.

Australia, meanwhile, taxes its residents on   worldwide income  . So the same income falls within both systems.

The treaty resolves that, usually by Australia giving a   foreign income tax offset   for Indonesian tax paid.

   What people get wrong

  "I paid tax in Indonesia so I do not report it in Australia."   Wrong. You report it and claim the offset.

  "It is offshore so Australia cannot see it."   Australia has extensive information exchange arrangements. This is not a strategy.

  "I will just not be an Australian tax resident."   Ceasing Australian tax residence is a substantive test about where you actually live and what ties you keep. It is not achieved by intention, and it has its own consequences including deemed disposal rules.

   What you actually need to do

  Report the Indonesian rental income on your Australian return
  Claim the foreign income tax offset for Indonesian tax paid
  Keep evidence of the Indonesian tax actually paid, because the offset depends on it
  Keep records of the purchase, because your Australian cost base matters even though Indonesia taxes differently

   On disposal

Indonesia applies a final tax on the   transfer value  . Australia calculates   capital gains   on the profit.

Those are different calculations on the same transaction, and the interaction is exactly where advice is worth paying for. Do not assume the Indonesian final tax covers your Australian position.

   The practical advice

Use an Australian accountant who has handled foreign property before, and an Indonesian adviser for the local side. One professional rarely covers both properly, and the gap between them is where m

t: Is Malaysia MM2H better than Bali?
s: Malaysia lets foreigners own freehold above state minimums and ties a long-stay visa to it. Bali offers neither. The trade-off is demand.
b:
Malaysia is the Southeast Asian outlier that most Bali buyers have never seriously looked at.

   What Malaysia allows

Foreigners can own property   freehold  , in their own name, subject to state level minimum purchase values and state approval. That is genuine ownership of land and building, not a lease or a right of use.

Malaysia My Second Home (MM2H) is the long stay programme. It has been repeatedly restructured with higher financial thresholds and tiered categories, so anyone considering it should check the current tier requirements rather than older summaries.

   Against Indonesia

    Malaysia   Indonesia  
                   
  Land ownership   Yes, above state minimums   No  
  Visa route   MM2H, property often required   Several, property not required  
  Term   Freehold or long leasehold   30 years, extendable  
  Tourism demand   Moderate, domestic heavy   Strong, international  
  Cost of living   Low   Low  
  English   Widely spoken   Widely spoken in expat areas  
  Healthcare   Strong private sector   Good routine, thin complex  

   The real trade

Malaysia gives you the thing Bali cannot: a title you own and can pass on without a disposal deadline.

What it does not give you is Bali's tourism engine. Villa rental demand in Malaysia is a fraction of Bali's, so the same money buys a more secure asset that earns considerably less.

There is also the state minimum purchase value, which in the popular states is high enough to push you well above what the same lifestyle costs here.

   Who should look at Malaysia

Anyone whose priority is owning something outright, passing it to children without a forced sale, and living somewhere cheap with good healthcare and English.

Anyone whose priority is rental yield should look at Bali and accept the weaker rights, or look at Thailand for a middle position.

   Common questions

    Can foreigners buy property in Malaysia?
Yes, freehold, subject to state minimum purchase values and state approval. It is one

t: Is Seminyak still worth buying in?
s: The most established foreign market on the island. Highest density, highest prices, almost no land, and the deepest resale pool.
b:
Seminyak was the first part of Bali to develop a genuine international property market, and it remains the most mature. That maturity is both the argument for buying here and the argument against.

   What Seminyak is now

Dense, built out, and commercial. The strip from Jalan Kayu Aya through Petitenget carries the island's deepest concentration of established restaurants, beach clubs, hotels and retail. Oberoi, Petitenget and Seminyak proper run continuously into one another.

There is essentially no undeveloped land left. What trades is existing buildings, and redevelopment means demolishing something to build something else.

The guest is older and higher spending than Canggu's, with shorter average stays. A large share comes from Australia and the Asian regional markets — Singapore, Malaysia, Korea, Japan — who want walkable dining, reliable service and a beach within a few minutes.

   The market

Land prices here are among the highest in Bali and the supply is fixed. When a parcel does trade it is usually privately and at a number that does not appear in any listing.

Most transactions are existing villas, many of them ten to twenty years old. The generation built during Seminyak's first boom is now at the age where pools, roofs, electrics and aircon all need work simultaneously. A villa that looks fine at a viewing may be a renovation project priced as a finished house.

Lease terms are frequently mid range, because a lot of the stock was leased for thirty years a decade or more ago. Remaining term varies enormously between apparently similar properties on the same street, and it is the first thing to establish.

   Rental performance

Strong, stable, and less volatile than Canggu. Occupancy holds better through shoulder season because the guest base is less trend driven, and the February trough is shallower than in areas depending on a narrower demand type.

Nightly rates at the upper end are among the highest on the island for well presented three and four

t: Is Airbnb legal in Bali?
s: Listing a villa nightly is a licensed commercial activity. Plenty of listings do not hold that licence, and enforcement has tightened.
b:
Short term letting in Bali is not a grey area in law. It is a licensed commercial activity with clear requirements. What is grey is enforcement, and that has been changing.

   What the law requires

Renting a property nightly to paying guests is   commercial accommodation  . It requires:

  Zoning that permits it.   The regional spatial plan classifies each parcel, and commercial accommodation is not permitted in every zone. A green or agricultural zone does not allow it, regardless of what the neighbours are doing.

  A business entity with the correct classification.   Under KBLI 2025 the accommodation activities have defined codes, and the entity operating the property must be registered for the right one via OSS with an NIB.

  Building permits that match.   PBG for the building, and SLF certifying it is fit for occupancy. A villa let commercially without SLF is operating outside the rules whatever else is in order.

  Operational licensing   appropriate to the accommodation type.

  Tax registration and filing   — income tax on the rental income, and the regional accommodation tax.

   The July 2026 change

  Bali closed new foreign owned villa and homestay registration to PMA companies with effect from 22 July 2026.  

This is the single most consequential development for foreign investors in this market. A plan that assumed setting up a PT PMA to operate short let villas has to be checked against current availability of the classification before it means anything, and a company holding a property it cannot lawfully operate is the worst outcome available: full compliance cost, no commercial benefit.

If you are being sold an off plan unit with a rental programme attached, ask specifically what entity will operate it, under what classification, and whether that classification is currently open. Get the answer in writing.

   The regional accommodation tax

There is a regional tax on accommodation — historically referred to as PB1 or PHR — charged on the accomm

t: Is solar worth it for a Bali villa?
s: The sunshine is excellent and the electricity bill is large, which makes the arithmetic better here than in most places owners come from.
b:
Bali sits near the equator with strong, consistent irradiance year round. Combined with an electricity bill driven by air conditioning and pool plant, that makes solar genuinely worth modelling.

   Why the load profile suits it

Solar generates during the day. A villa's daytime load is exactly what solar is good at:

  Pool pump, which runs for hours every day
  Air conditioning, heaviest in the afternoon heat
  Water pumps and heating
  General household load

That daytime alignment is the reason the economics work better here than for a house whose consumption is mostly in the evening.

   Cost and sizing

System cost scales with capacity. A villa system sized to cover a meaningful share of daytime load is a five figure investment in USD, with the exact number depending on panels, inverter, roof suitability and whether you add batteries.

Batteries roughly double the cost and are what let you ride through outages. Without them, a grid tied system stops when the grid does, which surprises owners who bought solar partly for resilience.

Given that short outages are routine here, the resilience argument is worth weighing rather than dismissing.

   Metering and export

Whether and how you are credited for exported power is set by regulation and has changed. Do not size a system on the assumption that generous export credit exists.

The safer design is one that covers your own daytime consumption well rather than one built to export surplus. Confirm the current rules before committing.

   Practical constraints

  Roof.   Orientation, pitch, shading from trees and neighbouring buildings, and structural capacity. Traditional alang alang thatch roofs are unsuitable, which affects a good number of villas here.

  Salt air.   Coastal installations need corrosion resistant mounting and more frequent inspection.

  Dust and ash.   Panels need cleaning. Volcanic ash events are infrequent but they matter, and dry season dust reduces output more than owners expect.

t: What is it actually like to work remotely from Bali?
s: The internet is better than the reputation. The legal position is worse than most people assume.
b:
Two separate questions get mixed together here. Can you physically work from Bali, and can you legally work from Bali. The answers are different.

   The infrastructure is fine now

  Fibre connections of 50 to 100 Mbps are standard   in the main expat areas. That is a genuine change from a few years ago, when the answer to this question was much less encouraging.

For calls, screen sharing and normal remote work, it is not a limitation.

What still catches people:

    Power cuts happen.   Usually short. A laptop with battery is fine, a desktop is not.
    Villa internet varies wildly.   The villa's connection is not the area's connection. Test it before you sign anything longer than a month.
    Get a local SIM immediately   with a decent data package. It is cheap and it is your backup when the villa connection drops mid call.
    Time zones.   Excellent for Asia and Australia. Workable for Europe with early starts. Genuinely hard for the US.

   The legal position

This is where it matters, and it changed this year.

In   April 2026   Indonesian immigration launched a dedicated Bali patrol task force. In its first three weeks it   detained 62 foreign nationals   for illegal work, overstays and document violations. Officers patrol Canggu, Ubud, Seminyak, Kerobokan and Uluwatu, and they check public social media and LinkedIn.

Working on a tourist visa is not a grey area and is being enforced. [The detail is here](/visas/bali visa crackdown 2026/).

   The permit that covers it

  E33G   exists specifically for people employed by or contracted to a company outside Indonesia. The published criteria are specific:

  A genuine foreign employment or consulting agreement
  Minimum annual income commonly cited at   USD 60,000  
  No income from Indonesian entities at all

It runs a year and renews while both conditions hold. [Full requirements here](/visas/digital nomad bali/).

   The thing nobody plans for

t: Do you need a prenup to own property in a mixed marriage?
s: Without one, a foreign spouse's interest can contaminate an Indonesian spouse's freehold. This is the most consequential document in a mixed marriage here.
b:
This is the single most important legal document for a foreigner married to an Indonesian citizen who intends to hold property, and it is routinely skipped.

   The problem

Under Indonesian marriage law, property acquired during a marriage is treated as joint marital property by default. Both spouses have an interest in it.

Hak Milik, Indonesian freehold, may only be held by an Indonesian citizen. Put those two rules together and the difficulty appears immediately: if an Indonesian spouse acquires freehold land during a marriage to a foreigner, the foreign spouse acquires an interest in a title a foreigner cannot lawfully hold.

The consequence is not theoretical. It can force disposal of the land, block the purchase at the notary stage, or surface years later on divorce, death or sale.

   What the agreement does

A prenuptial agreement separates the spouses' assets, so that property acquired by the Indonesian spouse is their own rather than joint. That removes the foreign interest and allows the Indonesian spouse to hold freehold normally.

It also protects the foreign spouse, by making clear what is theirs and what is not, which matters enormously if the marriage ends.

   If you are already married

Until 2015 the answer was that you were too late. The Constitutional Court decision in 69/PUU XIII/2015 changed that, and a   postnuptial   agreement separating assets is now possible.

It has to be properly executed before a notary and registered with the civil registry and, where relevant, noted so that it is discoverable. An unregistered agreement in a drawer does not do the job.

If you are already married, already here, and already own or intend to own land, this is the item to deal with before anything else.

   What it does not fix

A prenuptial agreement does not make a foreigner able to hold Hak Milik. Nothing does. It separates the estates so the Indonesian spouse can hold it cleanly in their own name.

t: What are NITKU and Coretax, and do property buyers need them?
s: Indonesia rebuilt its tax administration in 2025 and 2026. If your tax number is not linked correctly, filings and transfers stall.
b:
Indonesia replaced its tax administration system, and the change reaches property buyers through two identifiers that did not previously matter.

   The three numbers

  NPWP   is the taxpayer identification number. It has existed for decades and is what you need to file anything, receive taxed income, or complete a titled property transfer.

  NIK   is the national identity number carried by Indonesian citizens. Under the integration programme, an individual's NPWP is now the NIK — one number doing both jobs. For Indonesian citizens this happened automatically. For foreigners, who do not have a NIK, a sixteen digit NPWP is issued instead.

  NITKU   is the business unit identifier. A company has one NPWP and a NITKU for each registered place of business. If your PT PMA operates from more than one location, each needs its own NITKU, and invoices and filings must reference the right one.

   Coretax

Coretax is the administration platform that replaced the older filing systems. Registration, filing, payment, invoicing and correspondence all run through it.

Its practical significance is that it is far less tolerant of mismatched data than what it replaced. A name spelled differently on your passport and your tax registration, an address that does not match, an unlinked NPWP, or a missing NITKU produces a rejection rather than a phone call.

The rollout was rough. Through 2025 filings were delayed, invoices failed to generate and deadlines moved. By late 2026 it is substantially more stable, but the data matching strictness is permanent and is the part that affects you.

   Where it touches a property purchase

  Titled transfers.   BPHTB and the seller's disposal tax both run through the system. An NPWP that is not properly registered or does not match the identity documents will stall the transfer at the tax stage, after you have already committed.

t: What is the Bali property market doing in 2026?
s: Land in well-zoned coastal locations is holding. The standardised villa rental business built on it is where the pressure actually is.
b:
There are two markets here behaving differently, and most commentary confuses them.

   Land versus the business on it

  Land   in tourism zoned coastal locations is genuinely scarce. It cannot be manufactured, and it came through a complete tourism shutdown in 2020 and 2021 with prime locations intact. That scarcity is real and it supports price.

  The nightly rental villa business   depends on guest nights, achievable rates, licensing and competition. All four have moved against new entrants.

Calling the whole island overheated misses that the stress is concentrated in the second market.

   What is actually happening to supply

Construction of the standard three bedroom pool villa has run ahead of guest night growth in the main corridors. Pererenan and Cemagi in particular were rice fields in 2019 and are now dense with near identical product.

When two hundred functionally identical villas list in the same window, they compete on price, because nothing else separates them. That shows up first as softer nightly rates and higher vacancy, which is a yield problem before it is a valuation problem.

Differentiated property still performs. Generic property increasingly does not.

   The regulatory variable

In roughly one year: 18 business classifications closed to new foreign owned registration, facilitating nominee land arrangements criminalised, KBLI renumbered with a migration deadline, and a dedicated immigration task force deployed that detained 62 foreign nationals in its first three weeks.

Regulation moves faster here than the market cycle does, and it can strand a business model in a quarter. Anyone underwriting Bali purely on historical appreciation is watching the wrong variable.

   The 2021 stress test

The useful precedent already happened. Tourism stopped, income stopped, and a genuine distressed window opened where leaseholds and operating villas traded well below prior pricing.

Prime land came through it. Overleveraged operators did not. That is

t: Do you need a licence to drive a scooter in Bali?
s: Yes. And the reason it matters is not the police fine, it is what happens to your insurance claim.
b:
Almost everyone here gets around on a scooter. Most foreigners riding one are not properly licensed for it, and most of them have not thought through what that means.

   What you actually need

To ride legally you need either:

  An   International Driving Permit   endorsed for motorcycles, issued in your home country before you travel, alongside your home licence, or
  An   Indonesian licence (SIM)  , which you can apply for locally

The key detail is the   motorcycle endorsement  . A car licence plus an IDP that only covers cars does not make you legal on a scooter, and this is where most people are caught out without realising.

Rental shops will hand you a bike without checking any of this. That is not permission, it is just a shop that wants your money.

   Why it matters more than the fine

Police checks happen and the on the spot fine is an inconvenience.

  The real exposure is your insurance.  

A great many travel and health policies   exclude motorbike accidents unless you hold the correct licence   for the engine size you are riding. So the sequence that ruins people is:

1. Accident
2. Serious injury
3. Hospital, potentially evacuation
4. Claim denied because you were not properly licensed

Given that [medical evacuation to Singapore runs USD 55,000 to 100,000](/living/healthcare in bali/), that denied claim is not a paperwork problem. It is the most expensive consequence of a decision people make in about four seconds at a rental shop.

   Practical advice

  Get the endorsement before you fly.   Adding motorcycles to an IDP at home is cheap and quick. Doing it retrospectively is not possible.

  Wear a proper helmet  , not the token one the rental shop provides.

  Do not ride at night on unlit roads   if you can avoid it. Most of Bali outside the main strips has no street lighting.

  Rainy season changes everything.   Roads flood, drainage is inconsistent, and the surface goes slick within seconds of rain starting.

t: What is a representative office in Indonesia?
s: A foreign company can have a legal presence here without forming a PT PMA. It cannot earn revenue, which is the entire trade-off.
b:
Between doing nothing and forming a PT PMA sits a structure most people have never heard of.

   What it is

A representative office lets a   foreign company   establish a legal presence in Indonesia for defined non commercial purposes: market research, liaison, promotion, supervising the parent's interests.

It is an extension of the foreign parent, not a separate Indonesian company.

   The hard limit

  It cannot generate revenue.   No sales, no contracts producing income, no invoicing Indonesian customers.

The moment you want to trade, you need a PT PMA. That is not a grey area and it is the reason the structure is narrower than it first appears.

   Against a PT PMA

    Representative office   PT PMA  
                   
  Can earn revenue     No     Yes  
  Capital threshold   None of the PMA kind   Substantial, per classification and location  
  Setup burden   Lighter   Heavier  
  Ongoing compliance   Lighter   LKPM, monthly and annual filings  
  Can hold land   No   Yes, HGB  
  Supports investor KITAS   No   Yes  
  Can employ   Limited   Yes  

   Where it genuinely fits

A foreign company that wants boots on the ground before committing. Market research, building relationships, supervising a supply chain, or coordinating with Indonesian partners while the commercial decision is still open.

For a property buyer, it is usually   not   the right structure, because holding land needs HGB and that needs a PT PMA.

   Where people get it wrong

Using it to avoid PT PMA capital requirements while actually trading. That is operating without the right licence, and the classification closures of July 2026 have not made the authorities more relaxed about structure.

If revenue is the plan, the representative office is a staging post, not a destination.

   Common questions

    What is a representative office in Indonesia?
A legal presence for a foreign company covering research, liaison and promotion, without the ability to earn revenue.

t: Can foreigners buy property in the Philippines?
s: Foreigners can hold up to 40 percent of a condominium building and none of the land. Indonesia allows none of either, and still draws more capital.
b:
The Philippine rule is simple and strict: land is constitutionally reserved for Filipino citizens.

   What a foreigner can hold

  Condominium units  , provided foreign ownership stays within 40 percent of the building. Above that quota, no further foreign sales in that building.

  Buildings without the land  , through long term lease arrangements on the land beneath.

  Through a corporation   that is at least 60 percent Filipino owned, which carries the same nominee risk that Thailand and Indonesia now enforce against.

   Against Indonesia

    Philippines   Indonesia  
                   
  Land   Constitutionally reserved   Reserved for citizens  
  Condominium   Yes, within 40% of a building   Hak Pakai on strata, with conditions  
  Term on a unit   Perpetual   Term limited  
  Marriage route   Spouse may own, foreigner cannot   Requires asset separation agreement  
  Tourism demand   Domestic heavy, dispersed   International, concentrated  

The Philippine condominium is a stronger instrument than anything Indonesia offers on land, because it is perpetual. The constraint is that the market for it is thinner and more dispersed.

   Why the money still favours Bali

Philippine tourism is real but geographically scattered across thousands of islands, with weaker international flight connectivity to any single destination. Bali concentrates international demand in one place with one airport and a mature villa rental economy.

For a buyer whose return depends on filling a calendar, concentration matters more than constitutional generosity.

   The marriage trap, in both countries

A foreigner married to a Filipino citizen cannot circumvent the land rule through the spouse without creating problems. Indonesia has the same issue and a defined solution: a prenuptial or postnuptial agreement separating assets.

In both countries, treating a spouse as a convenient title holder is the same prohibited structure with more at stake than money.

t: How do you choose a developer in Bali?
s: Renders are free. What separates a developer worth paying is what they have finished, who they finished it for, and what they hold if it goes wrong.
b:
Off plan is the highest risk configuration in this market, and the developer is most of that risk.

   What to verify, in order

  One: what have they completed?   Not launched, not sold out. Completed and handed over. Visit it. Walk it. If the answer is "this is our first project," you are funding a learning curve.

  Two: who is the legal entity?   Many projects sit in a special purpose company formed for that project, with no assets beyond the project itself. If it fails, your contractual remedy is against an empty shell.

Ask for the company documents. Check who the shareholders and directors are, and whether the same people stand behind the completed projects they showed you.

  Three: does the land title exist, held by them, now?   Not "under acquisition." A developer selling units on land they have not secured is selling you their financing risk.

  Four: has PBG been issued for the design being sold?   If not, what is being marketed may not be what can lawfully be built.

  Five: what do previous buyers say?   Not the testimonials the developer selects. Find buyers from a completed project yourself and ask what slipped and how it was handled.

   The payment structure is the real protection

Tie every tranche to an   independently inspected milestone  , verified by someone you appointed and pay. Not the developer's project manager, not photographs.

Front loaded schedules transfer your leverage at the start. Once they hold most of the money, your ability to compel completion is whatever the contract gives you against a company that may hold nothing.

   Guaranteed returns

Ask who is guaranteeing them and what that entity holds. A yield guarantee from a project company with no other assets is worth what the company is worth when you call on it.

   The questions that end conversations

"May I see the land certificate and the PBG?" "Which completed project can I visit?" "Can I speak to a buyer you did not choose?" "Can payments follow inspected milestones?"

t: Is Jimbaran a good place to buy?
s: Closest established area to the airport, calmer than the west coast, and priced below both Seminyak and the Bukit clifftops.
b:
Jimbaran sits on the neck of the Bukit peninsula, ten to fifteen minutes from the airport, and it is consistently overlooked by buyers who go straight from Seminyak to Uluwatu without stopping.

   What Jimbaran is

A long sheltered bay on the western side, with a calm swimming beach, the seafood warungs that made the area famous, and a fishing fleet that still works. Inland it rises toward the Bukit, and on the eastern side it runs toward Nusa Dua.

The character is quieter and more residential than anywhere in the Canggu–Seminyak corridor. A mix of large resorts along the bay, established villa areas on the slopes, and genuine Indonesian neighbourhoods behind.

The bay faces west, which means sunsets, and it is sheltered, which means it is one of the few beaches in south Bali where swimming is easy and children are safe.

   The market

Land is cheaper than Seminyak and substantially cheaper than Bukit clifftop positions, and there is more of it. The hillside areas have genuine development land, and plot sizes are generous.

Stock ranges from older villas on large plots to newer builds, plus a significant amount of resort and branded residence product along the bay.

Lease terms at a given budget are longer than in the western corridor, and the elevation means a meaningful number of plots have ocean or bay views, which is the largest single rate multiplier available.

   Rental performance

Solid, steady and less seasonal than the west coast.

The guest profile skews toward families, older travellers and people in Bali for a specific reason — a wedding, a conference, a stopover, a first or last night before a flight. Average stays are shorter than Canggu's but the calendar is flatter.

Airport proximity is a genuine commercial asset and it is underrated. A villa that works for a first or last night captures bookings nobody else competes for, and the Bukit's traffic makes Uluwatu a forty five minute arrival while Jimbaran is fifteen.

t: What happens to your Bali property when you die?
s: A home country will does not settle an Indonesian land title, and heirs who cannot lawfully hold it face a disposal deadline.
b:
Most foreign owners here have never written this down, and the people who deal with the consequences are their families.

   The disposal rule

Indonesian land rights are tied to who may lawfully hold them. If a foreigner inherits a title reserved for Indonesian citizens, they generally must dispose of it within a set period. If they do not, the state's interest in it takes over.

That applies to a foreign spouse, foreign children, and anyone else who cannot hold the right in question. Grief plus a legal deadline plus a foreign language is a bad combination, and the deadline does not pause for any of it.

   Your home will is not enough

A will drafted in Australia, the UK or the Netherlands may be recognised in principle, but it does not by itself transfer or resolve an Indonesian land title. Practical problems follow immediately:

  Translation and legalisation of foreign documents takes time the deadline does not allow
  The executor has no standing here until it is established
  Bank accounts and company shares are separate questions from the land
  Where the title cannot be held by the heir, no will changes that

   What to actually do

  Write an Indonesian will covering Indonesian assets.   Keep it consistent with your home will so they do not contradict each other. Use an Indonesian notary.

  Know which right you hold.   Leasehold, Hak Pakai and HGB through a company all pass differently. A lease is contractual and should bind heirs and successors explicitly. HGB sits in a company, so the succession question becomes a shares question.

  Consider the company route deliberately.   Where property sits in a PT PMA, what passes is shares rather than land, which can be considerably simpler for foreign heirs. That is a real planning advantage and it is worth weighing when you choose the structure in the first place.

  Name someone here.   A trusted contact who knows which notary holds what, where the certificates are and who to call. Families lose months simply

t: Should you buy off-plan or completed in Bali?
s: Off-plan promises a discount and delivers construction risk, counterparty risk and a building nobody has inspected. Completed costs more and exists.
b:
The discount on off plan is real. So is everything you are accepting in exchange for it.

   The comparison

    Off plan   Completed  
                   
  Price   Lower, staged payments   Higher, paid at transfer  
  What you inspect   Renders and a show unit   The actual building  
  Construction risk   Yours   None  
  Counterparty risk   High. Often a project only company   Limited to the seller's title  
  Permits   May not be issued yet   Verifiable now, PBG and SLF  
  Income   Starts years away   Starts immediately  
  Specification   What the contract says, if enforced   What you can see and touch  
  Exit if things go wrong   A claim against an entity that may hold nothing   Sell the asset  

   The structural problem with off plan here

Many projects sit in a special purpose company formed for that project alone, with no assets beyond the project. If it fails, your contractual remedy runs against an empty shell.

Front loaded payment schedules make this worse, because once the developer holds most of your money your ability to compel completion is whatever the contract gives you.

   If you buy off plan anyway

  Verify the   land title exists and is held by the contracting entity now  , not "under acquisition"
  Confirm   PBG has been issued   for the design being sold
  Visit a project they have   completed and handed over  , not launched
  Speak to a buyer from that project you found yourself
  Tie every payment to an   independently inspected milestone  , verified by someone you appointed
  Treat any guaranteed return as worth exactly what the guaranteeing entity holds

   The case for completed

You can see it, survey it, check its permits against the building as it stands, look at twelve months of actual operating statements, and know precisely what you are buying.

You pay a premium for that. In a market where verification is the whole job and nothing protects you by default, that premium is usually money well spent.

t: What is Bali actually like in rainy season?
s: Roughly November to March. It is not the constant downpour people fear, and it is not the postcard either.
b:
Rainy season runs roughly   November to March  . Almost every article about Bali is written about the other six months.

   What it is actually like

It is not constant rain. That is the main misconception.

The pattern is typically heavy rain for a couple of hours, often in the afternoon, then it stops. Plenty of days are fine. Some weeks are genuinely wet.

What changes is everything around the rain:

  Humidity.   Persistent and heavy. Anything left in a cupboard grows mould. This is a real, ongoing, slightly demoralising feature of life here in those months.

  Flooding.   Low lying areas and poorly drained streets flood quickly. This is worth knowing before you rent or buy somewhere, because you will not see it in a dry season viewing.

  The roads.   Riding a scooter in heavy rain is genuinely unpleasant and meaningfully more dangerous.

  The sea.   Rougher, and rubbish washes onto west coast beaches. Photos from February look nothing like photos from July.

  Everything is quieter.   Fewer tourists, cheaper flights, less traffic. Some people prefer it enormously.

   Why this matters for property

  Occupancy drops in rainy season.   Any yield projection built on high season occupancy across twelve months is describing a year that does not exist. This is exactly why [the calculator asks for full year occupancy](/calculator/) rather than your best month.

  Construction slows.   Building through rainy season is harder and often more expensive.

  Drainage is a real question on any plot.   Ask what the land does in February. If the seller does not know, that is informative.

  Mould and maintenance are ongoing costs.   A villa in Bali needs more upkeep than the equivalent building in a dry climate, and refurbishment cycles are shorter.

   The advice I give most often

  Visit in February before you commit to anything.  

A single wet season visit tells you more about whether you want to live here than five dry season trips. It is also the only way to see how

t: Is North Bali worth buying in?
s: The cheapest coastal land on the island, black sand beaches, and a rental market that has not arrived. A long-horizon bet.
b:
North Bali runs along the Buleleng coast: Lovina, Singaraja, Pemuteran and the stretch toward the west. It is a different island from the south in almost every respect.

   What is actually there

Black sand beaches, dolphins offshore at Lovina, world class diving at Menjangan and Pemuteran, waterfalls inland, and dramatically fewer tourists than the south.

Singaraja is the old colonial capital and the second city of Bali, with a university and real local economy rather than a tourism economy.

   The price

Coastal land here is a fraction of Canggu, and often a fraction of Tabanan. It is the cheapest sea view land you can buy on Bali.

That discount is the whole thesis, and it exists because demand has not followed.

   The honest risk

Guests are few, seasons are short, and the drive from the airport is two and a half to three hours over the mountains. That drive is the single biggest constraint on North Bali's development, and it has been for decades.

A proposed North Bali airport has been discussed for many years. Treat it as a possibility rather than a plan, and do not price land on it. Buying land against an infrastructure project that may not happen is speculation on a government decision.

   Who it works for

People buying a home rather than a business. Retirees who want space, quiet and low cost and do not need the south. Divers. Anyone with a genuinely long horizon and capital they will not need back.

   Who it does not

Anyone underwriting rental yield. Anyone who may need to sell within five years, because the buyer pool is thin and slow. Anyone with children needing international schools or a family needing quick hospital access.

   What to check

  Zoning, since much of the coast is agricultural
  Access rights and road condition, which vary enormously
  Water supply, which is better than the Bukit but still parcel specific
  Realistic drive time to the airport at the hour you would actually travel
  Who the buyer is when you want to sell

t: Is Asia really cheaper on tax than Europe?
s: Europe adds a levy most years. Asia opens a door. The part people get wrong is that the tax follows the person, not the property.
b:
The comparison is real, and almost everyone draws the wrong conclusion from it.

   The direction of travel

  Europe   has been adding: wealth taxes in Norway, Spain and Switzerland, a property wealth tax in France, a deemed return system in the Netherlands, and the closure of most golden visa routes.

  Southeast Asia   has been opening: long stay visas in Thailand, Malaysia and Indonesia, no net wealth taxes, and in Indonesia's case no tax on the fact of owning at all.

   What Indonesia actually charges

  Event   Charge  
             
  Buying   Buyer transfer duty around 5 percent  
  Holding   Annual land and building tax, modest  
  Earning   Income tax on rental revenue  
  Selling   Final transfer tax on the sale value  
  Owning wealth   Nothing  

That is a different shape from a wealth tax. You are taxed when value moves or income arrives, not annually for existing.

   The mistake that costs people money

  Tax follows residence, not the asset.  

If you remain tax resident in Spain, Norway or the Netherlands, buying in Bali does not remove the property from your home country's calculation. Most European wealth taxes reach the worldwide assets of residents, and most income tax systems assess worldwide income.

Moving your money changes nothing. Moving yourself changes everything, and that is a serious decision involving exit taxes, tie breaker tests and genuinely living somewhere else.

Anyone selling a structure that supposedly delivers the tax outcome while you keep living at home is selling you an investigation.

   What a treaty does and does not do

Indonesia has treaties with most countries foreign buyers come from. They allocate taxing rights and relieve double taxation, usually by credit.

They do not remove the Indonesian obligation on Indonesian source income, and relief is not automatic. It requires a certificate of residence filed in the right form.
