Asia is genuinely cheaper on tax for people who actually move. For

t: Can foreigners get a mortgage in Indonesia?
s: Domestic mortgage lending to foreigners barely exists in practice, and leasehold is not mortgageable at all. Almost everyone pays cash or borrows at home.
b:
This is one of the biggest practical shocks for buyers arriving from markets where property finance is routine. Bali is a cash market, and the reasons are structural rather than temporary.

   Why the lending is not there

A bank lends against collateral it can register and, if necessary, seize and sell.

  Leasehold is not collateral.   Hak Sewa is a contract between you and a landowner. It is not registered at the land office and appears on no certificate. There is nothing for a bank to take security over, which is why no Indonesian bank will lend against a leasehold. Since the overwhelming majority of foreign purchases in Bali are leasehold, this alone removes most of the market.

  Hak Pakai is theoretically mortgageable   and practically difficult. It is a registered right and can carry a security interest, but bank appetite for lending to foreign individuals against it is very limited, and the requirements — residency, income documented in Indonesia, a track record with the bank — exclude most buyers.

  HGB held by a PT PMA   is the most financeable position, because the collateral is registered and the borrower is an Indonesian legal entity. Even then, lending to a young company with foreign shareholders and no domestic trading history is not something most banks will do. It becomes realistic once the company has two or three years of audited accounts and a banking relationship.

   What the terms look like when lending does happen

For the small number of cases that qualify, Indonesian rupiah lending rates run well above what buyers from Australia, the UK or Europe are used to. Loan to value is conservative, tenors are shorter, and currency risk sits with you if your income is not in rupiah.

That last point is the one people underestimate. Borrowing in rupiah against income in another currency, or the reverse, adds a genuine risk to a property investment that already has several. A rupiah move of fifteen percent against your home currency changes your effe

t: Do you need insurance for a Bali villa?
s: Building, contents and public liability are the baseline. The exclusions are where owners discover their policy does not do what they assumed.
b:
Insurance here is cheap relative to the asset and routinely either skipped or bought without reading.

   The cover you need

  Cover   Why  
             
  Building   Fire, storm, flood, structural damage  
  Contents   Furniture, appliances, electronics  
  Public liability   A guest injured on your property  
  Loss of rental income   Void period while damage is repaired  
  Employer liability   Staff injured at work  

Public liability is the one owners underrate. A guest drowning, falling on wet stone or being injured by a failing structure is a catastrophic exposure, and pools plus alcohol plus unfamiliar surroundings is a real combination.

   What voids or limits a policy

  Unpermitted construction.   An insurer can decline cover on a building without PBG and SLF, or on an extension that was never approved. This is the most common gap here, and owners discover it at claim time.

  Undeclared commercial use.   A policy written for a private residence may not cover a property operating as nightly accommodation. Declare the actual use.

  Unoccupied periods.   Many policies limit cover when a property sits empty beyond a stated number of days. Seasonal villas hit this.

  Maintenance and wear.   Gradual deterioration, damp and mould are usually excluded. In this climate that carves out a lot.

  Flood and seismic.   Sometimes excluded, sometimes an extension, sometimes limited. Bali is seismically active and low lying areas flood in wet season. Check specifically.

   The permit link

The connection between permits and insurance is the point worth internalising. PBG and SLF are not only a licensing matter. They are frequently the condition on which a claim is paid.

A villa without them is uninsured in practice even when a policy exists, which turns a permit problem into a total loss problem.

   Local versus international insurers

Local insurers are cheaper and understand local risk. Claims handling varies. International insurers with Indonesian operations

t: How does the Bali visa on arrival work?
s: Thirty days, extendable once for another thirty. It permits tourism and meetings, and nothing that counts as work.
b:
The visa on arrival is how most visitors enter, and the rules around it are simple until people start working on it.

   The basics

  Item   Position  
             
  Duration   30 days  
  Extension   Once, for a further 30 days  
  Maximum stay   60 days total  
  Where   On arrival at the airport, or e VOA online in advance  
  Eligibility   A published list of countries  

The e VOA applied for online before travel is generally the smoother route, because it lets you skip the payment queue on arrival.

   What it permits

Tourism, family visits, meetings, conferences, and looking at property. Buying property, meeting notaries, walking plots and signing as a buyer all sit comfortably within it. You are spending money, not earning it.

   What it does not permit

Work of any kind. Since the Dharma Dewata task force became operational on 15 April 2026, that has stopped being a theoretical distinction. Roughly 100 officers across Canggu, Ubud, Seminyak, Kerobokan and Uluwatu detained 62 foreign nationals in the first three weeks.

The test being applied is activity, not payment. Remote work for a foreign employer, yoga instruction, wellness workshops, unpaid volunteering and sponsored social posts have all been treated as work. A free villa stay in exchange for promotion counts as compensation.

   Extending

The extension is applied for before the initial 30 days expire, either online or through an agent. Leave time: applying on day 29 is how people end up overstaying because a document was wrong.

Agents charge a modest fee and handle the process. For a single extension it is usually worth it.

   Overstay

Fines accrue daily from the first day. Longer overstays escalate toward detention, deportation and a re entry ban. It is not a fee you can elect to pay in exchange for staying longer, and treating it that way has become considerably more expensive.

   When you need something else

If you intend to stay beyond 60 days, work remotely, run a business, retire he

t: What is a yayasan and can a foreigner run one?
s: The non-profit vehicle behind most schools, clinics and NGOs here. It cannot distribute profit, and using one to hold a business is a known trap.
b:
A yayasan is Indonesia's foundation structure, and a large share of the schools, clinics and community projects foreigners engage with are built on one.

   What it is

A non profit legal entity established for social, religious, humanitarian or educational purposes. It has founders, supervisors and managers rather than shareholders.

  It has no owners.   That is the defining feature and the source of every problem people create with it.

   The rule that matters

  A yayasan cannot distribute profit to its founders or managers.   Surplus must go back into the foundation's stated purpose.

People can be paid reasonable salaries for genuine work. What cannot happen is the foundation functioning as a business that quietly returns money to the people who set it up.

   Where foreigners use them legitimately

International and alternative schools. Clinics and health projects. Environmental and conservation work. Animal welfare. Community and education programmes.

Several of Bali's best known institutions are yayasan.

   The trap

Using a yayasan to run what is really a commercial business, because it appears to avoid PT PMA capital requirements and foreign ownership restrictions.

It does not work, for the same reason a nominee arrangement does not work: the structure exists to achieve something the rules prohibit, and the documents that make your control explicit are the evidence of it.

  You do not own a yayasan.   If the relationship with the Indonesian founders or managers breaks down, there is no shareholding to fall back on.

   If you are involved with one

  Understand whether you are a founder, supervisor, manager or employee, and what each carries
  Confirm the stated purpose matches what actually happens
  Check whether any foreign staff hold the correct work authorisation
  Keep the finances genuinely separate from any related commercial business

   The property angle

A yayasan is an Indonesian legal entity and can hold certain land rights for its purp

t: How do you sell a property in Bali?
s: Exit is the part nobody plans. Your buyer pool, your remaining lease term and your licence position decide the price far more than the villa does.
b:
Everyone models the purchase. Almost nobody models the exit, which is where the return is actually realised.

   Who can buy from you

This is the question that decides everything, and it is set on the day you buy.

  What you hold   Who can buy it  
             
  Leasehold with years remaining   Foreigners, and the shorter the term the smaller the pool  
  Hak Pakai   Foreigners with residency who meet the value threshold  
  HGB in a PT PMA   Buyers willing to take on a company, or buy the shares  
  Freehold via nominee   Nobody safely. The structure is the problem  

A leasehold with eight years left has almost no market. A leasehold with twenty five has a real one. The decay is not linear and it accelerates.

   What actually sets the price

  Remaining term  , if the title is term limited, and the quality of the extension clause.

  Licence position.   A villa that can lawfully sell nights is a business. One that cannot is a house with a pool. The gap is large.

  PBG and SLF.   Missing building approvals discount the price and shrink the buyer pool to people willing to take the problem on.

  Age of fit out.   Tropical wear is fast. A property due its five year refurbishment sells at the cost of that refurbishment, or below.

  Land, always.   Well zoned land in a good location is what holds value. The building depreciates.

   Selling through a company

If the property sits in a PT PMA you can sell the asset or sell the shares. Selling shares transfers the company, its licences, its history and its liabilities. It can be cleaner for the buyer and is often faster.

It also means the buyer inherits any compliance problems, so expect real scrutiny of the company's filings. Keeping the PT PMA properly compliant throughout is worth money at exit, not just peace of mind.

   Tax

The seller normally bears a final transfer tax on the sale value. Who pays what is negotiable in practice and should be explicit in the deed rather than assumed.

Where the property sit

t: What should you check at villa handover?
s: The last moment you have leverage is before you accept the building. After that, every defect is a favour you are asking for.
b:
Handover is a commercial moment, not a ceremony. Treat it accordingly.

   Before the day

  Retention should be held. If your contract has no retention, you have already given away your leverage
  Bring your independent surveyor or project manager, not just the builder
  Have the approved drawings and specification with you
  Have SLF in hand or a written date for it

   Structure and envelope

Roof, including from inside the ceiling void. Signs of water ingress at every junction. Wall cracks beyond hairline. Floor levels and drainage falls on terraces, which should run away from the building. Render and paint on the weather side.

   Water

Every tap, hot and cold, at pressure. Every drain, filled and released. Shower falls. Toilet flush and refill. Check under every sink after running it. Pool pump, filtration, lights and the balance tank if there is an infinity edge.

Run the whole house at once and see what the pressure does.

   Electrical

Every socket, every switch, every light. RCD tripping correctly. Electrical capacity sufficient for the villa running fully: air conditioning across all bedrooms plus pool pump plus kitchen. Undersized capacity is common and expensive to upgrade later.

Air conditioning units: cooling, draining, and no water marks below them.

   Joinery and finishes

Every door and window opening, closing and locking. Cupboard doors aligned. Insect screens. Tiling and stone for lippage and hollow sounds. Silicone lines.

In this climate, check timber for movement already visible at handover. If it has moved in the first months, it will keep moving.

   Documents

  Item   Why  
             
  SLF   Certifies the building is fit for use, and insurance may depend on it  
  As built drawings   You need them for every future repair  
  Warranties   Structure, waterproofing, pool plant, appliances, separately  
  Equipment manuals   Pool, pumps, air conditioning  
  Contractor contacts   Named people for each trade  

   The snagging list

t: What happens if you overstay in Indonesia?
s: A daily fine from day one, and past a certain point it stops being a fine and becomes detention and a re-entry ban.
b:
Overstaying is treated as an immigration offence rather than a billing matter, and the tolerance that once existed has narrowed considerably.

   How it escalates

  Situation   Consequence  
             
  Short overstay   Daily fine, payable on exit  
  Extended overstay   Detention, deportation, re entry ban  
  Deliberate or repeated   Longer ban, harder to reverse  

The daily fine is the visible part. The re entry ban is the part that ends plans, because it applies to Indonesia as a whole rather than to Bali, and it lasts years.

   Why people overstay

Almost never deliberately. The common causes are an extension applied for too late, a document rejected at the last moment, a medical problem, or simply miscounting the days.

The last one is more common than it should be. Count from the date stamped on entry, not from when you think you arrived, and treat the expiry date as the last day you may be in the country rather than the day you plan to leave.

   If it has already happened

Do not simply turn up at the airport and hope. Speak to a reputable visa agent or immigration directly, because how the situation is handled affects the outcome.

A short overstay disclosed and paid is a different matter from a long one discovered at the gate.

   The enforcement climate

The Dharma Dewata task force has been operational since 15 April 2026 with roughly 100 officers across the main expat areas, and it detained 62 foreign nationals in its first three weeks. Officers also monitor public social media and LinkedIn.

That posture applies to status generally, not only to working. Someone living here informally on rolling tourist visas while running a business is exposed on two fronts at once.

   Practical protection

  Diarise the expiry the day you arrive, not the week it approaches
  Start extensions at least a week before expiry, not on the last day
  Keep your passport and permit documents accessible
  If you live here, move onto the correct permit rather than cycli

t: What does $130,000 buy in Bali?
s: It is the number attached to Indonesia's Second Home route, and it buys very different things depending on where you point it.
b:
One hundred and thirty thousand US dollars is a useful benchmark because it sits near several thresholds at once.

   What it actually buys here

  Option   Realistic at this price  
             
  Leasehold land, inland or west coast   A decent plot with years on the clock  
  Leasehold villa, outer corridors   A small one or two bedroom, older stock  
  Apartment, strata title   A unit, with Hak Pakai possible if you qualify  
  Land plus build, Tabanan or inland   Plot plus a modest villa, if you supervise  
  Canggu or Seminyak villa   Not a chance  

The honest version: at this level you are buying either land somewhere early, or a small building somewhere established. Not both.

   Against the alternatives

Spain's golden visa wanted 500,000 euros before it closed. Portugal's property route is gone. Greece has raised thresholds sharply in prime areas. Dubai ties residency to a property value well above this.

So as a residency adjacent number, USD 130,000 in Indonesia is genuinely cheap. As a property number, it is entry level in a market where entry level means compromise.

   The trap at this price point

The temptation is a small villa in a developed corridor, marketed on yield. That is exactly the segment with the most competing supply and the softest rates.

The better use of this money is usually land in an area you have verified, held while the corridor develops, or a plot plus a build you actually supervise.

Both require patience. Neither produces income in year one.

   What to add to the number

Transaction costs of roughly 7 to 8 percent. Furnishing at USD 25,000 to 45,000 if it is a villa for rental. A cash buffer for a slow first year. If you are building, contingency of at least 15 percent.

A buyer who spends the entire 130,000 on the asset has under budgeted by a third.

   Common questions

    Can you buy a villa in Bali for $130,000?
Yes, in outer corridors or as older stock, typically small and leasehold. Not in Canggu or Seminyak.

    D

t: Is long-term rental better than Airbnb in Bali?
s: Short-term looks better on the headline rate and worse after costs, vacancy and licensing. For many owners the annual lease is the honest winner.
b:
The default assumption is nightly rental, because that is what the projections show. It is worth testing.

   The two models

    Short term   Long term  
                   
  Rate   High per night   Lower per month  
  Occupancy   Seasonal, 50 to 75 percent typical   Effectively 100 percent while leased  
  Costs   Staff, laundry, consumables, management, commission   Minimal  
  Wear   Heavy, constant turnover   Much lower  
  Licensing   Accommodation licence required   Different regime, generally simpler  
  Management   Intensive   Light  
  Cash flow   Lumpy, seasonal   Predictable, often paid a year up front  

   The arithmetic that surprises people

Short term gross revenue is genuinely higher. What closes the gap is everything underneath it.

Platform commission, management fee, cleaning and laundry per stay, consumables, full time staff, higher utilities, faster wear, a shorter refurbishment cycle, marketing, and the months where occupancy is 40 percent rather than 75.

Long term letting has almost none of that. A twelve month lease paid annually in advance, which is normal here, produces predictable net income with a fraction of the operational load.

Run both models on your actual property with honest numbers and the gap is often much smaller than the marketing suggests. On a generic villa in an oversupplied corridor, long term can win outright.

   The licensing dimension

Nightly accommodation is a licensed commercial activity, and Bali closed the villa and homestay classifications to new foreign owned company registration on 22 July 2026.

If your property cannot lawfully operate nightly, long term letting is not the fallback, it is the business. Price the property accordingly rather than on income it cannot legally earn.

   What long term costs you

Flexibility. You cannot use the villa yourself. You have less control over condition. Tenants live differently from guests, and a year of daily living leaves different wear than a series of three night

t: PT PMA or Hak Pakai for a Bali property?
s: One is a personal right that needs residency. The other is a company that needs a business. Choosing on cost alone is how people end up with the wrong one.
b:
Below about USD 250,000 almost everyone buys leasehold, because the alternatives cost more to set up than they save. Above it, this becomes the most consequential decision in the purchase, and it is usually made last.

   What each one is

  Hak Pakai   is a right of use, registered at the land office in your own name. It requires a KITAS or KITAP, applies to houses and apartments above a minimum value that varies by region and property type, and is granted for a defined term with a defined extension mechanism.

It is a personal right. You hold it, not a company. That is its main strength.

  HGB held by a PT PMA   is a building right, registered in the name of an Indonesian foreign investment company that you own. No residency requirement for you personally. The company holds the asset; you hold the company.

   The practical comparison

    Hak Pakai   HGB via PT PMA  
                   
  Residency needed   Yes, KITAS or KITAP   No  
  In whose name   Yours   Your company's  
  Setup cost   Low   Substantial  
  Ongoing cost   Effectively none   Accounts, tax filings, audits, corporate services  
  Commercial operation   No   Yes, if the KBLI is open  
  Value threshold   Yes   Capital requirements instead  
  Can be mortgaged   In theory, rarely in practice   Best of the three, still difficult  
  On your death   Passes, with rules on foreign heirs   Shares pass, subject to the same ownership rules  
  Exit   Sell the right   Sell the property or the company  

   When Hak Pakai is right

You hold residency or will. You intend to live in the property, or use it personally with occasional letting. You want the asset in your own name rather than behind a corporate structure. You do not want annual compliance.

It is the strongest position available to a foreign individual in Indonesia, and its limitation is that it is for living in, not for running a business from.

   When PT PMA is right

The property is genuinely a business — a villa complex, a commercial oper

t: What are the common property scams in Bali?
s: The losses here follow a small number of repeating patterns, and almost all of them happen before the deed is ever signed.
b:
Very little of what costs foreigners money in Bali is sophisticated. The same handful of patterns repeat, they are all detectable in advance, and the checks that catch them cost a fraction of what they prevent.

   The patterns

  The nominee.   Land bought in an Indonesian person's name, with a stack of side agreements — a loan, a mortgage, a power of attorney, a statement of trust — presented as giving you control. Indonesian courts have consistently held that arrangements designed to circumvent the foreign ownership restriction are void, so the side agreements do not save you.   Perda Bali 4/2026 now prohibits facilitating these arrangements  , which adds regulatory exposure to an already unenforceable position. When it fails, it fails completely.

  The seller who does not own it.   The person selling is a family member, a former owner, a broker who "represents the family", or someone with a power of attorney that has expired or was never valid. The certificate is real. Their authority to sell it is not.

  The certificate that does not match the land.   The document describes a parcel of a certain size and shape. The land you walked is a different size, or extends over a neighbour's boundary, or includes a strip that is actually a public road. Common on land that has been informally divided within a family over generations.

  The building with no permit.   A finished, beautiful villa with no PBG, or a PBG for a substantially smaller building. You buy it, and regularising it — or demolishing the excess — is your cost. In some cases it cannot be regularised at all because the zoning does not permit what was built.

  Zoning that does not allow your plan.   Land sold as a villa investment sitting in a green or agricultural zone where commercial accommodation is not permitted. The neighbours doing it anyway is not a defence and not a licence.

  The short lease sold as long.   Advertised as "eighty years", structured as thirty plus two extension options that are m

t: What is an are of land in Bali?
s: Land here is priced per are, which is 100 square metres. Confusing it with a square metre or an acre is an expensive arithmetic error.
b:
This sounds trivial and it is responsible for real mistakes, in both directions.

   The units

  Unit   Equals  
             
  1 are   100 square metres  
  1 hectare   100 are, or 10,000 square metres  
  1 acre   roughly 40.5 are  
  1 tumbak or ubin   around 14 square metres, older local usage  

Land in Bali is quoted   per are  . A plot described as 5 are is 500 square metres. A price of "USD 60,000 per are" on a 5 are plot is USD 300,000, not USD 60,000.

   Where the errors happen

  Assuming a price is total rather than per are.   The single most common one, and it is off by the number of are in the plot.

  Confusing are with square metre.   A factor of one hundred.

  Comparing per are prices across areas without adjusting for what you get.   Two plots at the same price per are can be worth wildly different amounts depending on zoning, access and shape.

Always restate the number yourself: total price, total square metres, and price per square metre. Do the arithmetic rather than accepting the framing you were given.

   Leasehold is quoted differently

A leasehold may be quoted as a total for the full term, or per are per year. These are not comparable without knowing the term.

A plot at "USD 3,000 per are per year" for 25 years on 5 are is USD 375,000 across the term. Quoted as a lump sum it might have looked like a different proposition entirely.

Establish: total price, term in years, what happens at extension and at what cost.

   What to check alongside the number

Price per are means nothing without the rest:

  Zoning designation, which can change value several times over
  Access road width and whether the right of way is registered
  Shape and frontage, since awkward plots build badly and sell worse
  Buildable envelope after KDB, KLB, green area and setbacks
  Whether the stated area matches the certificate and the ground

That last one matters. Have the boundaries walked against the certificate. Stated areas and actual areas do not always a

t: What is it like moving to Bali with children?
s: Families live in a completely different Bali to everyone else, and it costs roughly three times as much.
b:
Almost every article about living in Bali is written by and for single people in their twenties. If you have children, most of that advice does not apply to you.

   The budget is a different bracket entirely

A comfortable single expat lives on roughly   USD 1,800 to 2,500 a month  . A family with children in international school should plan for   USD 4,000 to 6,500  .

The gap is almost entirely school fees. [Budget USD 8,000 to 28,000 per child per year all in](/living/international schools bali/) once registration, transport, uniform and lunch are added to tuition.

That single line changes every other decision you make here.

   The order that works

  1. Pick the school.  
Not the area. The school. Curriculum, waiting list, and whether it leads where you want your child to go afterwards.

  2. Rent near it.  
Bali traffic makes a 12km school run an hour each way, twice daily. Families who choose the beach first and the school second spend their lives in the car.

  3. Live there a year.  
Through a rainy season. Watch how the family actually handles it, not how the holiday version felt.

  4. Only then consider buying.  

Doing this in reverse ties a large amount of capital to the wrong side of the island, and moving is much harder once you own something.

   What families need that others do not

  Hospital proximity.   Serious care is in Denpasar. Being ninety minutes away is a different proposition at 3am with a child than it is on a spreadsheet. [Healthcare and insurance detail here](/living/healthcare in bali/).

  Insurance with evacuation cover, per person.   Check the child limits specifically, they are sometimes lower.

  Space and safety at home.   Pools without fencing are standard here and are the obvious hazard with small children.

  A car, not just scooters.   Which means checking road access to any property properly.

  Community.   This is the one that decides whether families stay. School communities are where it comes from, which is another

t: Can you buy property on the Gili Islands?
s: Three small islands with real tourism demand, no cars, limited fresh water, and a land market that rewards caution over enthusiasm.
b:
The Gilis sit off northwest Lombok: Trawangan, Meno and Air. They are administratively part of West Nusa Tenggara rather than Bali, and they are small enough that everything about them is constrained.

   The three islands

  Gili Trawangan   is the largest and busiest, with the bars, dive shops and most of the accommodation.

  Gili Air   is the middle option, with a growing residential and long stay community and a calmer feel.

  Gili Meno   is the quietest and least developed, aimed at couples and people who want nothing to happen.

   The legal position

The same national framework applies as everywhere in Indonesia. No freehold in a foreign name, with leasehold, Hak Pakai for those with residency, or HGB through a PT PMA.

Land title on the Gilis has historically been more complicated than on Bali. Customary holdings, incomplete registration and competing family claims are more common. Verification through a notary you appointed, against the land office record, is not optional here.

   The constraints

  Constraint   Reality  
             
  Fresh water   Very limited. Desalination and shipped water are normal  
  Electricity   Improved via undersea cable, still fragile  
  Waste   A genuine and visible problem on small islands  
  Transport   No motor vehicles. Everything moves by cart, bicycle or boat  
  Medical   Basic only. Anything serious means a boat to Lombok or Bali  
  Construction   Every material arrives by boat, which changes the cost base  

Building here costs meaningfully more than on Bali for exactly that last reason, and timelines are longer.

   Demand and risk

Tourism demand is real and has recovered strongly. It is also concentrated, seasonal, and dependent on boat conditions. Rough seas cancel crossings, which cancels arrivals you had already counted.

The 2018 Lombok earthquakes caused serious damage and a collapse in visitors that took years to recover. That is not a reason to avoid the islands, but it belongs in the risk assessment

t: How does the Indonesian spouse visa work?
s: Marriage to an Indonesian citizen opens a residence route, and eventually KITAP. It does not by itself grant the right to work.
b:
Marriage to an Indonesian citizen is one of the more straightforward routes to long term residence here, and one of the most misunderstood in what it actually permits.

   What it gives you

A sponsored residence permit, with the Indonesian spouse as sponsor. It allows you to live here, and after qualifying periods it opens the path to KITAP, permanent stay.

For people building a life here rather than passing through, it is the most stable status available short of citizenship.

   What it does not give you

The right to work, automatically. A dependent or spouse sponsored permit grants residence, not employment. Working without separate authorisation is a violation and is being enforced on the same basis as everything else since April 2026.

This catches trailing spouses in particular. Someone who moved here with a partner, has time, and starts teaching classes or taking freelance work is working, whether or not it feels like a job.

   The property problem nobody mentions

This is the part that matters most and gets least attention.

Indonesian law treats property acquired during a marriage as joint marital property by default. Hak Milik, freehold, may only be held by an Indonesian citizen. Put those together and an Indonesian spouse buying freehold during a marriage to a foreigner creates a genuine legal problem, because the foreign spouse acquires an interest in a title they cannot lawfully hold.

The solution is a prenuptial agreement separating assets, or a postnuptial agreement where you are already married, which became possible after Constitutional Court decision 69/PUU XIII/2015.

It must be executed before a notary and properly registered. An agreement signed and filed in a drawer does not do the job.

If you are married to an Indonesian citizen and intend to own land, deal with this before anything else.

   Documentation

Marriage certificates issued abroad generally need legalisation and translation to be recognised here. Start that early, because it

t: What permits do you need to build on leased land in Bali?
s: The permit is applied for in the landowner's name in most cases, which means your right to build has to be written into the lease before you sign it.
b:
Most foreign funded building in Bali happens on leased land, and the permit structure is where it most often goes wrong. The problem is not that it cannot be done. It is that the paperwork runs through the landowner and buyers sign leases that do not account for that.

   Who the permit belongs to

A   PBG  , the building approval that replaced the IMB, is issued in relation to the land and generally applied for by or with the consent of the party holding the land right. On leased land that is normally the Indonesian landowner, not you.

This has three consequences that must be handled in the lease itself.

  You need the landowner's cooperation to apply.   If the lease does not oblige them to sign what the application requires, they can simply decline, and you own a lease over land you cannot lawfully build on.

  The permit follows the land.   When the lease ends, the building and its permit stay. That is normal and it is why the term and the extension clause matter more than the build quality.

  A landowner who will not cooperate has leverage.   Mid build, that leverage is close to absolute. This is a known pattern and it is entirely preventable at the drafting stage.

   What the lease must say

Before you sign, not after:

  An express right to build  , describing the scale and nature of what you intend, not a general permission.

  An obligation on the landowner to sign   every application, consent and document required for the PBG, the SLF, utilities connections and any operational licence, within a defined time, without additional payment.

  A power of attorney   allowing you or your appointed agent to make the applications, so cooperation is not required afresh at every step.

  Clarity on who owns the building   during the term and what happens to it at the end. Under Indonesian practice the building generally follows the land at expiry unless the contract says otherwise, which is why the extension clause is the value.

  A right to sublease or assign  ,

t: What occupancy should you expect in Bali?
s: Peak months fill themselves. The annual number is decided in the shoulder and wet season, which is exactly what projections skip.
b:
Occupancy is the single most sensitive input in any Bali yield model, and the one most often borrowed from somebody else's property.

   The shape of the year

  Period   Demand  
             
  July to August   Peak. Rates and occupancy both highest  
  December to early January   Strong, holiday driven  
  April to June   Good shoulder, dry and pleasant  
  September to October   Good shoulder  
  November, February, March   Weakest. Wet season, thin demand  

The peak fills itself. Anyone can sell July. The annual figure is decided by what happens in February, and that is precisely the month sales material does not discuss.

   The new listing problem

A brand new listing does not achieve area average occupancy. It has no reviews, no ranking, and no repeat guests. Platforms surface established listings ahead of new ones.

Expect a materially weaker first year while reviews accumulate. Owners who modelled year one at stabilised occupancy are the ones who run out of working capital in month eight.

   What drives it beyond season

  Differentiation.   In a corridor with two hundred near identical three bedroom pool villas, the ones that fill are the ones that are not identical. A view, a size the market is not building, a genuinely distinct design.

  Photography.   Guests book from images. Professional photography is among the highest return spend on the whole property.

  Reviews.   Ranking follows them, bookings follow ranking, and the first ten matter disproportionately.

  Location within the area.   Walkability to a beach or a cafe strip beats being 400 metres further out by more than the price difference suggests.

  Price discipline.   Discounting to fill February trains the algorithm and your returning guests to expect that rate.

   How to model it honestly

Take the area's stabilised occupancy, month by month rather than annually. Reduce year one substantially. Apply your realistic rate by month rather than a blended annual figure.

Then calculate break

t: Can a foreigner open a bank account in Indonesia?
s: With a KITAS it is straightforward. Without one it is mostly not possible, and the workarounds sold to tourists carry real risk.
b:
A local account makes daily life dramatically easier: paying staff, utilities, contractors, rent and taxes without international transfer fees on every transaction.

   What you need

  Status   Position  
             
  KITAS or KITAP holder   Standard account available at most banks  
  Visitor visa   Generally not possible at a normal branch  
  Company (PT PMA)   Corporate account, required for the business  

The requirement almost everywhere is a valid stay permit plus supporting documents. Passport, KITAS, tax number where applicable, proof of address and sometimes a reference or sponsor letter.

   The main banks

BCA is the most widely used and has the best app and ATM network. Mandiri and BNI are state banks with wide branch coverage. Permata and CIMB Niaga are often more comfortable with foreign customers.

Branches differ more than banks do. One branch may refuse what another accepts, so if the first attempt fails it is worth trying elsewhere before concluding it is impossible.

   The tourist workaround, and why to avoid it

Agents in Bali will offer to open an account for someone on a visitor visa, for a fee. These accounts typically carry balance caps, sit outside the normal KYC process, and can be frozen without much warning.

If your purpose is to hold money for a property purchase, that fragility is exactly what you do not want. Transfer from your home account directly instead, which is normal, traceable and perfectly workable for a purchase.

   Transferring money in

For a property purchase, send by bank transfer from an account in your own name to the registered owner or the notary's designated account. Keep the transfer confirmation, the contract clause it corresponds to, and the receipt.

Large transfers are exposed to the exchange rate and to your bank's spread, which on a property sum can exceed your legal fees. Specialist transfer services generally price better than a high street bank.

   Cards and daily payments

Local debit cards work

t: Is it cheaper to build in Bali than Australia?
s: Over 1,500 Australian builders collapsed in a year and buyers lost deposits. Building here costs a fraction, and the risks are entirely different ones.
b:
The comparison comes up constantly with Australian buyers, and both halves of it are real.

   The cost gap

    Bali   Australia  
                   
  Per square metre   USD 600 to 1,500   Several times that  
  Pool, standard   USD 15,000 to 25,000   Substantially more  
  Labour   Abundant, low cost   Scarce, expensive  
  Contractor availability   Good   A genuine constraint  
  Timeline, standard villa   9 to 12 months after permits   Often longer  

At standard specification a 200 square metre villa here is roughly USD 200,000 to 240,000 for the building. The same brief in Sydney or Melbourne is not comparable.

   The Australian problem

Builder insolvency has been severe, with over 1,500 construction firms collapsing in a single year and buyers losing deposits on incomplete homes. Combined with a housing shortfall of around 315,000 dwellings, the pressure is structural rather than cyclical.

That is what pushes people to look offshore.

   The Bali problem

Different, and not smaller.

  You do not own the land  , so you are building on a lease, a Hak Pakai, or through a company. The lease must clearly authorise construction and deal with what happens to the building at expiry.

  Permits are the long pole.   PBG before you start, SLF on completion. Building without PBG risks stop work orders and, where it breaches zoning or setbacks, demolition.

  Supervision is on you.   Owners who manage remotely through photographs sent by the builder find problems at handover that cost more than supervision would have.

  Exclusions eat the budget.   The per square metre rate typically excludes pool, landscaping, furniture, air conditioning, boundary walls, professional fees and utility connections. Add those and a "200,000" villa lands nearer 280,000.

   The honest verdict

Building here is genuinely much cheaper and genuinely more exposed. In Australia the risk is that your builder fails. Here the risk is that you built the wrong thing on land you cannot use that

t: What does a notary do in a Bali property purchase?
s: The PPAT executes the deed and registers the transfer. Using the seller's notary is the cheapest way to lose your only independent check.
b:
In most of the world you would have your own lawyer. In Indonesia the equivalent function sits with a notary, and the single most consequential decision in your transaction is whose notary it is.

   Notaris and PPAT

  A Notaris   is a public official authorised to draw up authentic deeds: contracts, company formation documents, powers of attorney, leases, wills.

  A PPAT   —  Pejabat Pembuat Akta Tanah  — is specifically authorised to execute deeds transferring registered land rights and to lodge them with the land office. A PPAT has a defined territorial jurisdiction.

Most practitioners hold both appointments, which is why the terms get used interchangeably. The distinction matters because only a PPAT can execute an   AJB  , the deed of sale and purchase for a registered right, and only a PPAT with jurisdiction over that area can do it for that parcel.

A leasehold, by contrast, is a notarial deed rather than a land office transfer, because Hak Sewa is not a registered right.

   What they actually do

  Verify the title   against the land office record: parcel number, area, boundaries, registered owner, encumbrances.

  Confirm the seller's identity and authority  , including spousal consent where the seller is married, since jointly held property cannot be disposed of without it.

  Check encumbrances   — mortgages, caveats, registered rights, existing leases.

  Draft the deed   in Bahasa Indonesia, which is the version that governs regardless of any translation.

  Calculate and handle the taxes  : BPHTB for the buyer, income tax on the seller's disposal.

  Execute the deed   with both parties present, or under a valid power of attorney.

  Register the transfer   at the land office and obtain the updated certificate.

What they do not automatically do is advise you on whether the deal is good, negotiate on your behalf, or run the deeper checks — zoning against the spatial plan, permits, access, customary constraints — unless you instruct and pay for them.

t: What are the building rules in Bali?
s: Height limits, setbacks, coverage ratios and local custom all constrain what you can build, and the customary rules are not written in the spatial plan.
b:
Bali constrains building more than most of Southeast Asia, and the constraints come from three separate places: national and provincial regulation, the regency spatial plan, and the customary rules of the village you are building in. All three bind.

   The height limit

Bali applies a building height limit that is famously tied to the height of a coconut palm and is generally applied at fifteen metres. In practice this means most buildings are limited to roughly three storeys.

It is the rule most responsible for Bali looking the way it does, and it is enforced. Exceptions exist for specific structures and specific zones, but they are exceptions, and a design that assumes one will be granted is a design at risk.

The practical effect on a villa project is that you build outward, not upward. Land area, not floor count, determines what you can deliver. That is why plot size matters so much more here than in markets where you can add a storey.

   Coverage: KDB and KLB

  KDB  , the building coverage ratio, caps the proportion of your plot that the building footprint may occupy. Depending on the zone this commonly sits in the range of forty to sixty percent, and lower in green and agricultural zones.

  KLB  , the floor area ratio, caps total floor area across all storeys relative to plot size.

These two decide the real capacity of your land. A five are plot in a zone with a fifty percent KDB gives you 250 square metres of footprint, and the rest must stay open. That open area is your pool, garden and parking — which is fine, because those are what a Bali villa sells on.

Buyers routinely calculate a build from plot size alone and are then surprised by the KDB. Do it the other way: check the zone's KDB and KLB first, then design.

   Setbacks

Several apply at once.

  Road setback   — distance from the road boundary, varying with the road's classification.

  Boundary setbacks   — distance from neighbouring parcels, particularly where there are openings.

  Sempadan

t: Can you bring a pet to Bali?
s: Bali is a rabies control zone, and the honest answer is that bringing a dog or cat in is restricted and difficult, not simply expensive.
b:
This is the question that catches families late in a move, usually after the flights are booked.

   The core problem

Bali has an ongoing rabies control programme. Because of it, the province has applied restrictions on bringing dogs and cats onto the island that are considerably tighter than the rules for Indonesia generally.

The practical consequence is that people commonly route pets into Jakarta or another entry point and then face a separate, restricted question about moving the animal onward to Bali. That second step is where plans fail.

Do not assume it is a matter of paperwork and fees. Verify the current position with the Indonesian agricultural quarantine authority before you commit to anything, because this has changed more than once and the rules that applied to someone two years ago may not apply to you.

   What the process generally involves

  Step   Typical requirement  
             
  Microchip   ISO standard, implanted before vaccination  
  Rabies vaccination   With a validated certificate  
  Titre test   Blood test at an approved laboratory, with a waiting period after  
  Import permit   Applied for in advance  
  Health certificate   From an official vet in the origin country, close to travel  
  Quarantine   On arrival, duration depending on origin and route  

Timelines here are long. The titre test and its waiting period alone can push preparation to six months, so this belongs at the start of a relocation plan rather than the end.

   Use a specialist

Pet relocation to Indonesia is not a do it yourself process. A specialist relocation agent who moves animals into Indonesia regularly will know the current entry position, the approved laboratories and the realistic timeline.

Pick one that will tell you plainly if it cannot be done, rather than one that takes a deposit and works it out later.

   The harder question

If your animal is old, brachycephalic, anxious, or unwell, weigh the flight itself seriously. Long haul cargo travel in

t: How many tourists visit Bali?
s: Arrivals have recovered past pre-pandemic levels. Villa supply has grown faster, which is why more visitors has not meant better yields.
b:
Visitor numbers are the input everyone quotes and almost nobody uses correctly.

   The recovery

Tourism collapsed to effectively nothing in 2020 and 2021. It recovered through 2022 and 2023 and has since passed pre pandemic levels, with foreign arrivals running in the millions annually alongside a very large domestic market.

The headline story is genuinely positive. The useful question is what it means for a specific property.

   Why more arrivals has not meant better yields

Because accommodation supply grew faster.

Between 2021 and 2026, an enormous volume of villa construction happened in the Canggu and Pererenan corridor, much of it the same three bedroom pool villa. Guest nights rose. Available villa nights rose faster.

That is the entire explanation for why owners report softer rates against a backdrop of record arrivals. The market grew; your slice of it got thinner.

   Where the visitors come from

Australia has historically been the largest single source market, with India, China, Singapore, Malaysia, South Korea, the UK, Russia and Europe all significant. The mix shifts, and it matters:

  Australian visitors skew toward shorter, higher frequency trips
  European visitors stay longer, often through the dry season
  Regional Asian markets are more sensitive to flight capacity and pricing

A property positioned for one market is exposed to that market's currency, flight routes and economic conditions.

   Domestic tourism

Often overlooked and substantial. Indonesian visitors from Jakarta and Surabaya fill weekends and holidays with a different pattern from foreign guests, and they are less sensitive to international disruption.

Properties that appeal only to Western guests forgo that.

   How to use the numbers

Not as reassurance. Arrivals tell you the size of the pool, not your share of it.

The questions that matter are: how many comparable properties compete within a kilometre, how many were added in the last two years, and how many are under co

t: What should you ask a Bali property agent?
s: Most agents will answer what you ask and not much more. These are the questions that surface the problems before you pay a deposit.
b:
Agents here are not regulated the way they are in most Western markets. There is no licensing body with teeth, no standard disclosure obligation, and commission structures vary widely.

That does not make them dishonest. It means the burden of asking is entirely on you.

   About the title

  What exactly is the title type, and may I see the certificate?
  Who is the registered holder, and are they the person selling?
  How many years remain, and what does the extension clause actually say?
  Are there registered charges over the land?
  Is there a spouse, and have they consented?
  Has this land passed through inheritance, and is that resolved?

   About the land

  What is the zoning designation on this specific parcel?
  What is the buildable envelope after KDB, KLB, setbacks and green area?
  How wide is the access road, and is the right of way registered?
  What happens here in wet season?
  What is the water supply, and what does it cost in full occupancy?

   About the building

  Do PBG and SLF exist, and do they describe the building as it stands?
  Were any extensions approved?
  When was it built, and when was it last refurbished?
  What is the electricity capacity?

   About the income, if it is sold as an investment

  May I see twelve months of actual operating statements, not a projection?
  What occupancy did it achieve, month by month?
  Does an operating licence exist, and does it transfer with the sale?
  What is the full cost base including staff, management and platform commission?
  Is there a sinking fund, and what does refurbishment cost?

   About the transaction

  Who is the notary, and may I appoint my own?
  What is the payment schedule, and what conditions attach to each tranche?
  Is the deposit refundable, and on what defined grounds?
  Which account do funds go to, and is it in the registered owner's name?
  What are the total closing costs?

   About the agent

  Who pays your commission, and how much is it?
  Do you represent the s

t: Is East Bali worth buying in?
s: Rice terraces, Mount Agung, almost no tourism infrastructure, and prices a fraction of the south. A lifestyle buy more than a yield play.
b:
East Bali covers Karangasem regency and the Sidemen valley: terraced rice, river gorges, Mount Agung dominating the skyline, and a pace that has not changed much.

   What is there

  Sidemen   is the valley that draws most foreign interest: dramatic terraces, a handful of boutique properties, and genuine quiet twenty minutes from anywhere commercial.

  Amed   on the northeast coast is a diving area with black sand beaches and a small, established foreign community.

  Candidasa   is an older, faded resort area with reasonable infrastructure and low prices.

  Around Mount Agung  , the villages are agricultural and largely untouched by tourism.

   The price

Land here is a fraction of the south, and often below Tabanan. For the money you would spend on a small Canggu plot you can buy something with a view of a volcano and a valley.

That is the appeal, and it is real.

   The honest limitation

Rental demand is thin and seasonal. Guests who come to Sidemen come for a few nights of quiet as part of a wider trip, not for a two week villa holiday.

The drive from the airport is around two hours. Amenities are limited: no international schools, limited medical, few restaurants outside the boutique properties.

Underwrite rental income conservatively or not at all. If your case depends on nightly yield, this is the wrong part of the island.

   Volcanic risk

Mount Agung is active. The 2017 and 2018 eruptions closed the airport repeatedly and caused evacuations within the exclusion zone.

That risk is manageable and mostly affects the immediate slopes, but it belongs in the assessment: insurance treatment, evacuation zones, and the effect on tourism when it happens.

   What to check

  Zoning, since almost everything here is agricultural
  Access road width and condition, which varies enormously
  Water supply, generally better than the south but parcel specific
  Distance to the exclusion zones around Agung
  Realistic drive times to the airport and to a hospital

t: What visa do you need for business meetings in Indonesia?
s: It covers meetings, negotiations and site visits. It does not cover doing the work, and that line is being enforced.
b:
The business visa sits between tourism and employment, and the boundary is narrower than most people assume.

   What it covers

Meetings, negotiations, contract discussions, conferences, exhibitions, site inspections, supplier visits and due diligence. Activities where you are representing a foreign company and not performing work inside Indonesia.

For a foreign buyer visiting notaries, inspecting land and meeting contractors, either a visitor visa or a business visa is generally appropriate depending on the specifics.

   What it does not cover

Performing work. Delivering services to an Indonesian client. Managing local staff day to day. Taking up a role in an Indonesian company. Earning income sourced in Indonesia.

The distinction is between   discussing   business and   doing   it. Attending a meeting about a construction project is covered; supervising the site as its project manager is not.

   Single and multiple entry

Single entry suits a one off trip. Multiple entry, valid over a longer period with a maximum stay per visit, suits anyone travelling here repeatedly.

For a buyer running a project remotely with several visits a year, multiple entry is usually the practical choice.

   The enforcement context

Since the Dharma Dewata task force became operational on 15 April 2026, activity rather than payment has been the test applied. Roughly 100 officers across Canggu, Ubud, Seminyak, Kerobokan and Uluwatu detained 62 foreign nationals in the first three weeks.

A business visa is not a workaround for working here. Someone using one to run an Indonesian operation day to day is exposed in exactly the same way as someone working on a tourist visa.

   When you need something else

If you are taking a role in a PT PMA, a work KITAS or investor KITAS is the correct instrument. If you are employed by an Indonesian entity, a work permit is required.

If you are working remotely for a foreign employer while here, the E33G is the route, not a business visa.

t: Can foreigners buy property in Jakarta?
s: The same national rules apply, but the market is apartments, tenants are corporate, and nobody is buying it for the lifestyle.
b:
Almost every foreign buyer looking at Indonesia looks at Bali. Jakarta is the country's actual economy, and it works completely differently.

   What a foreigner can hold

The same framework as everywhere in Indonesia. No Hak Milik. In practice, for Jakarta, that means   strata titled apartments under Hak Pakai   for those who qualify on residency and minimum value, or property held through a PT PMA.

Apartments are the realistic instrument here. Landed housing is effectively a local market.

   How it differs from Bali

    Jakarta   Bali  
                   
  Stock   High rise apartments   Villas and land  
  Tenant   Corporate expatriates, professionals   Tourists, long stay foreigners  
  Demand driver   Employment and business   Tourism  
  Seasonality   Minimal   Severe  
  Yields   Moderate, steadier   Higher headline, more volatile  
  Supply   Substantial oversupply in segments   Corridor specific oversupply  
  Liquidity   Deeper local buyer pool   Foreign buyer pool  

The critical difference: Jakarta has a   domestic   buyer and tenant market. Bali's depends on foreigners arriving.

That makes Jakarta less exciting and less fragile.

   The honest assessment

Jakarta apartment oversupply has been a persistent feature in several segments, and yields reflect it. It is not a market that rewards buying the newest tower on a launch discount.

What it does offer is corporate tenancy, no tourism seasonality, and an economy that exists independently of whether people want a holiday.

   Who should look at it

Anyone whose interest in Indonesia is economic rather than lifestyle, and who wants income that does not depend on a booking calendar.

Anyone who wants a villa, a pool and a life should not be looking at Jakarta at all, and mostly is not.

   Where foreigners actually buy

  SCBD and Sudirman   hold the corporate towers and the highest value apartments, with tenants from banking, energy and multinationals.

  Kuningan   covers the embassy district and mu

t: Is Sumba or Labuan Bajo the next Bali?
s: Spectacular, genuinely early, and separated from Bali by a decade of infrastructure. The phrase next Bali does more harm than good here.
b:
Both get pitched as the next Bali. Both are worth understanding on their own terms rather than through that comparison.

   Sumba

An island east of Bali, roughly twice the size, with a fraction of the population and almost no tourism infrastructure. Wild coastline, megalithic villages, a living traditional culture and one globally famous luxury resort that anchors the island's reputation.

Genuinely beautiful and genuinely remote. Flights are limited, roads are poor, and medical facilities are basic.

   Labuan Bajo

The gateway town to Komodo National Park on western Flores. Tourism here is real and growing, driven by liveaboard diving and Komodo day trips, and the government has designated it a priority destination with airport and infrastructure investment.

More developed than Sumba, considerably less than Bali.

   The comparison that matters

    Bali   Labuan Bajo   Sumba  
                         
  Flight connections   Extensive international   Domestic, growing   Limited  
  Tourism volume   Millions   Meaningful, growing   Very small  
  Infrastructure   Strained but present   Developing   Minimal  
  Medical   Good routine   Basic   Basic  
  Build cost   Low   Higher, logistics   Much higher, logistics  
  Resale pool   Deep   Thin   Almost none  

   The honest position

The ownership rules are identical: no freehold for foreigners anywhere in Indonesia. What differs is everything commercial.

Building costs more because materials ship in. Operating costs more because skilled staff are scarcer. Demand is smaller and more seasonal. And the exit is the real problem, because the pool of people who want to buy on Sumba and can lawfully do so is very small.

   Who this suits

Operators with capital they do not need, who will be present, running something themselves, on a ten year view.

It does not suit passive investors, and the "next Bali" framing is what gets people into trouble. Bali took fifty years and an airport.

   Common questions

    Can fore

t: How do you make a Bali villa listing perform?
s: In a corridor of near-identical villas, photography and the first ten reviews decide your occupancy more than the building does.
b:
When two hundred comparable villas list in the same area, guests are not choosing on merit. They are choosing on the first three photographs.

   Photography is the highest return spend

A professional shoot costs a small fraction of a single month's revenue and affects every booking for years. It is the clearest positive return available to a villa owner and it is routinely skipped in favour of phone photos.

What matters:

  Shot at the right time of day, which for a Bali villa usually means early morning and blue hour
  The pool as the hero image, because that is what guests are buying
  Wide but honest. Distorted lenses that oversell produce disappointed reviews
  Styled: towels, flowers, table set, lights on
  Every bedroom and bathroom, because guests who cannot see a room assume the worst
  Some sense of the surroundings, so people understand where they are

Reshoot after refurbishment. A listing showing a fit out you have since replaced is undervaluing your own asset.

   The listing text

Lead with what is unrepeatable about the property, not with adjectives. "Twelve minutes' walk to Batu Bolong, rice field view that cannot be built out" beats "stunning luxury villa" every time.

Answer the questions guests actually ask: how far to the beach, is there air conditioning in every room, is there fast wifi, is parking available, is it quiet at night. Listings that answer these get fewer wasted enquiries and better matched guests.

Be accurate about the road. A villa down a rough lane will get reviewed on it regardless of whether you mentioned it, and mentioning it filters out the guests who would have complained.

   The first reviews matter disproportionately

New listings have no ranking. The first ten reviews establish it, and the algorithm compounds from there.

That argues for launching deliberately: price below your target for the first weeks, over deliver on service, and ask satisfied guests to review. It is short term revenue traded for long term ranking

t: Do you need an architect to build in Bali?
s: The design decides your build cost, your permit and your nightly rate. It is the cheapest part of the project and the one people cut.
b:
The most expensive decision in a Bali build is made on paper, months before anything is poured, and it is routinely handed to whoever the contractor recommends.

   Why the design matters more here

In a market where the villa competes on photographs, the design is the product. Two villas on adjacent plots with identical build costs can achieve nightly rates twenty or thirty percent apart, entirely because one was designed to photograph and live well and the other was drawn to fit rooms onto a plot.

The design also determines whether you clear the permit. A PBG application requires proper technical drawings and structural calculations assessed against the zone's KDB, KLB, height limit and setbacks. A drawing that ignores any of those is a rejected application and months lost.

And it determines cost. The difference between an efficient structural grid and an inefficient one is commonly ten to fifteen percent of the build, which dwarfs the entire design fee.

   What it costs

Architectural fees in Bali typically run   five to ten percent of construction cost   for a full service — concept, developed design, technical drawings, permit documentation and construction supervision.

Cheaper arrangements exist. A drafter producing permit drawings from a layout you specify costs a fraction of that, and for a simple, conventional building it can be adequate. What you lose is the design thinking, the material knowledge and the supervision.

On a USD 300,000 build, a full architectural service at seven percent is USD 21,000. If it improves the nightly rate by fifteen percent on USD 60,000 of annual revenue, it repays itself in under three years and keeps paying for the rest of the term.

   What good looks like in Bali specifically

  Climate.   Cross ventilation, deep overhangs, orientation away from the worst of the afternoon sun, and drainage that handles a tropical downpour rather than an average rainfall figure. Bali buildings fail on water and heat more than anything e

t: Where should you live in Bali if you surf?
s: The swell window decides which coast works when, and that should decide where you buy far more than the marketing does.
b:
Surf is why a large share of the foreign population is here, and it is a legitimate input into where to buy, because being twenty minutes from your break in traffic is not the same as being five.

   The two coasts and the two seasons

Bali's geography gives it surf all year, because the coasts face opposite ways.

  Season   Wind   Works best  
                   
  Dry, roughly April to October   Offshore southeast   West coast: Bukit, Canggu, Kuta  
  Wet, roughly November to March   Offshore northwest   East coast: Nusa Dua, Sanur, Keramas  

Dry season is the classic Bali season, with the Bukit breaks at their best. Wet season pushes everyone east, and the east coast breaks are generally more advanced and more exposed.

   The main areas

  The Bukit   holds the famous waves: Uluwatu, Padang Padang, Bingin, Impossibles. Reef breaks, powerful, mostly for confident surfers. Living on the Bukit means the best dry season access and a long drive to everything else.

  Canggu and Echo Beach   are beach and reef breaks, more forgiving, extremely crowded. This is where most surfing foreigners live, and the crowding is the trade off for convenience.

  Kuta and Legian   are beach breaks and the best place to learn, with sand bottom and surf schools.

  Sanur and the east   come alive in wet season, with reef breaks that suit stronger surfers.

  Medewi  , on the west coast in Jembrana, is a long left and far quieter, though a long way from everything.

   What this means for buying

If surfing is genuinely a priority, buy on the coast that works in the season you will be here most. Someone here through European summer wants the west coast. Someone here December to March should look east.

Then drive it. Being three kilometres from a break sounds close and is twenty five minutes at the hour you would actually go.

   The safety part

These are reef breaks, and the reef is shallow and sharp. Currents at Uluwatu and Padang Padang are strong and have caught experienced surf

t: What is an EPO and do you need one?
s: Ending a KITAS is a process, not a departure. Leaving without closing it properly causes problems on your next application.
b:
People plan the arrival carefully and improvise the departure. The departure is the part that affects whether you can come back cleanly.

   What an EPO is

Exit Permit Only. Where you hold a KITAS and intend to leave permanently rather than return, the permit is formally cancelled and an exit permit issued, allowing you to depart with your status properly closed.

Historically this was a distinct document. The process and terminology have been simplified and changed over time, so confirm the current requirement rather than relying on how it worked for someone a few years ago.

   Why it matters

An unclosed permit is an open record. It can create difficulties when you next apply for an Indonesian visa, complicate the sponsor's position, and leave loose ends around tax registration and company roles.

If your KITAS was sponsored by a company or a spouse, leaving without closing it also leaves obligations sitting with that sponsor.

   What else to close

Leaving properly is more than immigration.

  Item   Action  
             
  KITAS or KITAP   Cancel and obtain the exit permit  
  Tax   Deregister or file appropriately for your NPWP  
  Company   Resign roles, or close the PT PMA properly if it is dormant  
  Staff   Terminate lawfully, with severance calculated correctly  
  Bank accounts   Close, or understand what happens when your permit lapses  
  Utilities and leases   Give notice and settle  
  Property   Decide whether to sell, lease out, or appoint a manager  

   The company you leave behind

A dormant PT PMA does not stop existing because you left. Reporting obligations continue accruing, penalties compound, and the eventual cost of regularising or closing it exceeds maintaining it would have.

If the venture is over, close the company properly. That takes time, so start before you leave rather than after.

   Property held while non resident

Hak Pakai requires valid residency. If you hold it and your permit lapses, there are consequences to understa

t: Should you ship your belongings to Bali?
s: Sea freight takes months and attracts duty. For most people the honest answer is to bring two suitcases and buy the rest here.
b:
The instinct is to ship everything. For most people moving here it is the wrong call, and the reasons are practical rather than sentimental.

   Why shipping usually loses

  Furniture is cheap and good here.   Bali has a large furniture industry. Teak, rattan, custom joinery and upholstery are made locally at prices well below Europe, Australia or North America, and the styles suit the climate.

  The climate destroys imported furniture.   Humidity warps veneered board, delaminates glued joints and grows mould in upholstery. Furniture built for a dry temperate house does not enjoy a Bali wet season.

  Electrical goods do not match.   Indonesia runs 230V at 50Hz on European style plugs. North American appliances need transformers. Warranties do not travel, and local service for a foreign model is difficult.

  Duty and clearance.   Personal effects can attract duty depending on your status and how the shipment is declared, and clearance is a process rather than a formality.

   What is worth bringing

  Clothing, especially anything hard to find in your size
  Specialist professional equipment and tools
  Laptops, cameras, hard drives
  Prescription medication with documentation
  Documents: certificates, apostilled paperwork, medical records
  Anything genuinely irreplaceable or sentimental

   What to leave

  Furniture, in almost all cases
  Large appliances
  Books, which mould here
  Bedding and towels, which are cheap locally and better suited to the climate
  Anything you have not used in a year

   If you do ship

Sea freight is the only sensible option for volume, and it is slow: expect a couple of months door to door depending on origin, plus clearance time.

Use an agent experienced with Indonesian customs. Have a detailed inventory with values. Ship after your stay permit is settled rather than before, since your status affects what relief is available.

Insure it. Salt air, handling and long transit are hard on a container.

   The arithmetic

t: Can you get a mortgage in Bali?
s: Foreign buyers here are effectively cash buyers. Local lending is largely closed and the alternatives carry their own problems.
b:
This surprises buyers who are used to markets where financing is routine. Plan on cash.

   Why local lending is largely closed

Indonesian banks lend against titles they can enforce against. A foreigner cannot hold freehold, and the alternatives are harder security:

  What you hold   Financeable locally  
             
  Leasehold   Rarely. It is a contract, not a registered title  
  Hak Pakai   Occasionally, on restrictive terms  
  HGB via PT PMA   More possible, still difficult, and rates are high  

Where lending is available at all, expect a large deposit requirement, a short term, and interest rates well above what you would pay in Europe, Australia or North America.

   The realistic alternatives

  Release equity at home.   Borrowing against property in a country with a functioning mortgage market, at that market's rates, and bringing the cash here. This is what most buyers actually do and it is usually the cheapest capital available.

  Developer payment plans.   Common on off plan projects. These are not really financing, they are staged payments to a developer, and they carry the full off plan risk profile: you are funding construction against a contract with an entity that may hold nothing.

  Private and seller lending.   It exists. It is unregulated, expensive, and enforcement if things go wrong is difficult. Treat it as a last resort and take independent legal advice on the security arrangement.

   Why this matters beyond the purchase

Being a cash market has consequences for the whole market, not just for you.

It thins the buyer pool at exit, because your buyer also needs cash. It makes prices less sensitive to interest rates than most property markets. And it means distress does not show up as forced sales the way it does elsewhere, so price discovery is slower and less reliable.

That last point is worth holding onto when you assess what a property is "worth". Asking prices in a cash market can drift a long way from transacted prices without a

t: Singapore, Hong Kong or Bali?
s: Both let foreigners own outright and both charge heavily for the privilege. Bali offers neither ownership nor the entry cost.
b:
Singapore and Hong Kong are where regional capital is parked. Bali is where some of it goes to be spent.

   The ownership position

  Singapore.   Foreigners can buy condominiums freely. Landed residential property is restricted and requires approval. The barrier is not permission, it is   Additional Buyer's Stamp Duty  , which for foreign buyers is severe and deliberately so.

  Hong Kong.   Foreigners can buy, subject to stamp duties that have been used as a cooling tool for years, though some were relaxed as the market softened.

  Bali.   No ownership at all for foreigners. Lease, Hak Pakai or HGB through a company.

   What that actually means

Singapore and Hong Kong do not stop you owning. They price you out with duty. Indonesia does not charge you much and does not let you own.

Those are different systems producing a similar outcome: the foreign buyer holds less than a local does.

   The comparison

    Singapore   Hong Kong   Bali  
                         
  Foreign ownership   Condos yes, landed restricted   Yes   No  
  Entry barrier   Very high stamp duty   High stamp duty   Low  
  Entry price   Very high   Very high   Low  
  Yields   Low   Low   Higher, more volatile  
  Rule of law   Excellent   Strong   Verification is on you  
  Liquidity   Deep   Deep   Thin, foreign dependent  
  Currency   Stable   Pegged   Volatile  

   Why Singapore money buys in Bali

Not as an alternative to Singapore property. As a different asset class entirely.

A Singapore based buyer is not choosing between a Singapore condominium and a Canggu villa. They already have the first and want the second for cash flow, lifestyle, or both, at an entry price that is a rounding error against Singapore prices.

That is why the flow exists and why it is relatively insensitive to Bali's ownership restrictions. The capital is not looking for security. It has security at home.
